For the full schedule, see this [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/203539-Season-25-Schedules/#post1397056][b]forum post[/b][/url].

notes.title: Learning Points and How To Use Them
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/b714336bc22a27e16e0522a6fb1be02f0d7312a2.png[/img]

Developing your character in Albion Online is a journey with many possibilities, and Learning Points can help you progress essentially [b]five times as quickly[/b]. This guide shows how Learning Points work, how to earn them, and how to use them wisely to advance in the areas that matter to you.

[h3]What are Learning Points?[/h3]
Learning points, ([b]LP[/b] for short) allow your character to [b]accelerate progress[/b] considerably on the [b]Destiny Board[/b].

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/fad636fec00c66899ecc7453261602b70654943f.jpeg[/img]

Once you’ve reached [b]at least 20% of progress[/b] in a given node (a mastery level of a specific skill), you’ll unlock the option to immediately complete that level by spending Learning Points. This is indicated by a line in the progress bar of a given node.
[list]	[*]Open the Destiny Board (Hotkey: B)[/*]	[*]Select the node you wish to learn[/*]	[*]Click “[b]Learn[/b]” to spend the necessary Learning Points and complete that level[/*][/list][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/3475725d699bf2161820a6ca83112717d0c03036.jpeg[/img]

The amount of Learning Points needed to complete a node depends on the [b]amount of Fame [/b]that would otherwise be required to complete it. It also[b] scales with the type and level of the node [/b]you wish to complete. Each Learning Point counts for more Fame at higher levels on the Destiny Board.

To automatically learn a node without having to go through this process every time, you can activate [b]Auto-Learn[/b]. This will use Learning Points in the selected nodes once the 20% threshold has been reached. For this to work, you need to have Auto-Learn selected in both the node you wish to progress, as well as the main Auto-Learn option located at the [b]top-right of the Destiny Board[/b]. Here you can also see your current amount of Learning Points.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/d27bf11e9a75978706deaa032e98403a6e055a94.jpeg[/img]

[h3]How do I get Learning Points?[/h3]
Learning Points can be obtained in several ways:
[list]	[*]You [b]automatically earn 30 LP every day[/b] by having active [b]Premium [/b]status	[list]		[*]With Premium you receive 1 point every 48 minutes, whether you’re online or not[/*]	[/list][/*]	[*]You will also receive [b]500 Learning Points[/b] the first time you purchase [b]7 days Premium or more[/b] for a character[/*]	[*][url=https://albiononline.com/mastery-packs?utm_source=lpguide][b]Mastery Packs[/b][/url] contain different amounts of Learning Points, depending on the tier you purchase[/*]	[*]Non-Premium characters can earn [b]10 Learning Points[/b] by completing the [b]daily Adventurer’s Challenge[/b][/*]	[*]You can obtain [b]Tomes of Learning[/b] by completing certain [b]Albion Journal missions[/b].	[list]		[*]These reward a certain amount of Learning Points when used, depending on their tier[/*]	[/list][/*][/list][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/4b02ca55e22f4f1fddb5b31a35505c933b6f7e20.jpeg[/img]

There is [b]no limit[/b] to how many Learning Points you can accumulate, so you might want to save them for the right opportunity.

[h3]How can I use Learning Points?[/h3]
Learning Points can be used to progress in most areas of your Destiny Board.

[b]Combat[/b]

You can spend Learning Points on Weapon/Armor mastery to [b]unlock[/b] the ability to use [b]higher-tier items[/b]. If used on the specialization nodes on the outside of the Destiny Board, you can boost your [b]Item Power[/b] of each item.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/1003c272131e2dc76d99190765043133a677a8b0.jpeg[/img]

[b]Tip: [/b]Since combat Fame is comparatively easy to come by in Albion, you may want to consider using your Learning Points on other areas that you wish to progress first.

[b]Crafting[/b]

Similarly to combat, crafting mastery allows you to [b]craft higher-tier items[/b], while specialization reduces [b]Focus[/b] costs and increases the chances of crafting [b]higher quality[/b] items.

[b]Tip: [/b]It is often recommended to use Learning Points to progress through lower-level crafting specializations, allowing you to unlock more valuable, higher-level crafting easily.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/5345a716790028356c45546e10584f301c84bd85.jpeg[/img]

[b]Refining[/b]

When it comes to [b]refining,[/b] the first level within a node unlocks the ability to refine a new tier of materials. After that, additional levels [b]increase your Focus efficiency[/b].

[b]Tip: [/b]If you’re interested in refining, it’s often recommended to use Learning Points to increase your specialization and become a master refiner.

[b]Gathering[/b]

[b]Gathering nodes[/b] work like refining. Reaching the first level of a node will [b]unlock a new tier of gathering tools and gathering armor,[/b] while further levels within a node increase the gathering speed and yield of resources within that tier.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/a6f3a4eb107930eb1e71945e4f941feaa9fdd22b.jpeg[/img]

[b]Tip:[/b] Gathering is a great place to use Learning Points early on. It is often recommended to use Learning Points [b]to unlock the first level[/b] of a new gathering tier, so that you can use better tools and gathering armor while starting to progress towards the next tier.

Learning Points [b]can not[/b] be used to boost progress through the [b]Adventurer and Reaver[/b] nodes, nor on [b]cooking, alchemy, and farming[/b].

How you spend your Learning Points is ultimately up to you, and really depends on the activities you want to do in Albion. And remember, if at any point you’re unsure, you can always hold onto your Learning Points for now and use them later. Happy learning!

notes.title: Dev Talk: UI Improvements
notes.content:
After our last Dev Talk on the upcoming [url=https://albiononline.com/news/dev-talk-open-world-improvements][b]open-world changes[/b][/url], [b]Game Director Robin Henkys [/b]sat down to explore the other side of the [url=https://albiononline.com/update/horizons][b]Horizons[/b][/url] update: its UI improvements. In this video, we look at the much-anticipated customization options and quality-of-life improvements coming when the update releases on [b]October 28[/b].

[previewyoutube=SRCmznJAMCI?rel=0;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3]Advanced Inventory Options[/h3][list]	[*]Collapse your equipped items into a [b]compact view[/b]	[list]		[*]This gives you more room to see what’s in your inventory[/*]	[/list][/*]	[*][b]Adjust the size[/b] of items in your inventory[/*]	[*]New [b]sorting[/b] options:	[list]		[*]Weight[/*]		[*]Tier[/*]		[*]Estimated market value[/*]		[*]Value by weight[/*]	[/list][/*][/list][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/52bd9ce121f731d8bbb0dcbe4a8133ceee6397bf.png[/img]

[h3]Storage Upgrades[/h3]
The following features are being added to Bank and Chest UIs:
[list]	[*]A [b]Move All [/b]option	[list]		[*]Allows you to easily move items between your inventory and the bank, or between bank tabs[/*]	[/list][/*]	[*]A [b]Repair All[/b] function	[list]		[*]Lets you repair items from within bank tabs[/*]	[/list][/*][/list][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/d11d2e2c00c90aba0cc01b94616631920abb3186.png[/img]

[h3]Quick Settings Presets[/h3][list]	[*][b]Create and save [/b]settings presets with your preferred graphics, audio, and control options[/*]	[*]Presets can have [b]keybindings [/b]to switch instantly in different gameplay situations[/*][/list][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/66f2b48731d727b59abad7fa3ef1d901ab31154c.png[/img]

[h3]HUD Editor[/h3][list]	[*]Adjust the [b]position, scale, and opacity[/b] of nearly every HUD element[/*]	[*]Some elements have [b]additional customization options[/b][/*]	[*]Export and import layouts to [b]share[/b] your setups with other players[/*]	[*]Assign HUD layouts to a [b]Quick Preset[/b] to get the perfect interface for any activity with a single keystroke[/*][/list][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/5a6f80ece6848406a12ab13e2f019b3d2b7a432d.png[/img]

These changes will enhance your gameplay experience and provide a level of convenience and customization never before seen in Albion. Stay tuned for our next Dev Talk where Robin will introduce the new Albion Journal categories and their rewards!

In the meantime, learn more about the Horizons update in the [url=https://albiononline.com/update/horizons][b]official update page[/b][/url].

notes.title: Guide: Farming
notes.content:
When you attend to your farms after a hard day’s adventuring, you’re not just taking a well-deserved break. You’re also fueling Albion’s [b]economy[/b] as you produce [b]raw materials[/b] that are used in a multitude of ways across the game.

[previewyoutube=xVEXsDiEkVA?rel=0;full][/previewyoutube]
Farmed products are used to create many different kinds of [b]food and potions[/b]. Food is essential to keep [b]crafting stations[/b] running, and also provide [b]buffs[/b] to players when consumed, while potions offer additional options in [b]combat[/b]. You can read more about them in our [url=https://albiononline.com/news/guide-potions-alchemy][b]guide to potions and alchemy[/b][/url][b].[/b]

In addition, you can use your farm to raise [b]baby animals[/b] to become the [b]mounts[/b] that accompany every adventurer on their journeys.

This article provides you with a step-by-step guide for you to get started, before going through the different types of farming. Ready to start growing your own crops, herbs, and animals? Then read on…

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/54a4c23445df17ba1ebc8c2c77e3ca3372f11f46.jpeg[/img]

[h3]Step 1: Purchasing an Island[/h3]
In order to farm, you need a [b]farming plot[/b]. This is most common on a [b]player island,[/b] but can also be on a [b]farming territory[/b] provided by a guild.

Islands can be purchased at the [b]Island Merchant[/b] in any of the Royal Cities, Caerleon, or Brecilien. The Island Merchant is located in the center of these cities, close to the Marketplace. Here’s how it appears on the region map:

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/43ca6ac296d02f665d04156c1c99e5646a4b61a5.jpeg[/img]

Please note that to purchase an island you need at least [b]7 days of Premium[/b]. After this, you can [b]keep the island forever[/b] without needing to continuously have Premium status.

Every island is [b]linked to the city[/b] in which it was purchased, and you can own up to one island for each city. They share a biome, and importantly you can travel between an island and its host city [b]for free[/b]. If you wish to travel from an island to a different city, you need to pay [b]transportation costs[/b].

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/f9bc6ba1811caf8b0135f345619e3de0753b3796.jpeg[/img]

Now that you have an island, you can travel to it using the Travel Planner.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/e6959654a300c968e8e0a5c40827ab7b552722c9.jpeg[/img]

[h3]Step 2: Building a Plot[/h3]
Depending on the level of your island, you will have access to a number of [b]multipurpose plots[/b] that can be used for different types of farming plots or buildings. A[b] level 1 island [/b]contains one multipurpose plot[b]. Farming territories[/b] have only four plots to build on but will produce four times as much crop yield, and will grow animals four times as quickly.

To start building a farm, go to a multipurpose plot. Then, navigate to the Build UI by clicking your avatar in the top cleft and selecting ‘Build’ (on desktop you can simply [b]press H[/b] to open this menu). Navigate to the second tab, “Farming”, where you can choose between building a [b]Farm, Herb Garden, Pasture, or Kennel[/b]. Each of these allows you to grow different crops or raise different animals.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/82586a2f6bb7aacd8c699105602224765f0145ac.jpeg[/img]

To build one of these, you need to make sure you have the necessary resources, which you can buy on the Marketplace or gather yourself.

[h3]Step 3: Growing Produce[/h3]
Let’s say you want to farm carrots. Once you’ve built a farm plot, you need to purchase some Carrot Seeds. Level 2 islands contain a [b]farming merchant [/b]from whom you can buy seeds, or you can obtain them from Marketplaces. It might be worth comparing prices to see which option is cheaper.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/df6299a3876b129951a3409b82a4aa7d2f6f2f56.jpeg[/img]

Go to your farming plot, select the Carrot Seeds from your inventory, and click "Place" to plant them.

If you have [b]Focus[/b] [b]Points, [/b]you can choose to [b]water your plants[/b] which will guarantee that you receive seeds back from your crops (see below). If you water about half your plants, you can maintain enough seeds for the next day without having to purchase new ones, increasing your profits.

[h3]Step 4: Harvesting[/h3]
All plants have a [b]growth cycle of 22 hours,[/b] after which you can harvest them. There is also a chance that you’ll receive additional [b]seeds[/b] that you can use to farm again, and [b]Earthworms [/b]which can be used to craft Fishing Bait.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/951c4c0bcf73a7f0efaa66ab5ff463b6bfc76d2a.jpeg[/img]

Go to your farming plot and click “Collect”. Congratulations, you've successfully grown and harvested your first plants!

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/cce19b83c896714f96a70e5a9229ba114459fd91.jpeg[/img]

You can now sell your crops at the Marketplace, or use them for crafting food.

[h3]Types of Farms & their Products[/h3]
Specializing in a particular type of farming can allow you to progress more quickly in that area, leading to greater [b]efficiency[/b] and [b]mastery[/b] over time. Conversely, [b]diversifying[/b] your farming operations lets you produce a [b]broader range of items[/b], offering flexibility and adaptability in the market. Each farming plot has a fixed cost and can be demolished at any point, which returns 90% of its resources. Below is an overview of the costs of each plot type and their products:

[b]Livestock Animals[/b]

Livestock placed on a [b]pasture[/b] need to be fed in order to start growing. Each type has a [b]favorite food [/b]which [b]halves[/b] the amount of crops necessary to feed them.

Livestock Animals’ growth cycle is [b]1 day 20 hours,[/b] but can be [b]halved[/b] if you have [b]Premium[/b] [b]Status[/b].

When fully grown, these animals can either be collected to be [b]butchered,[/b] or fed again in order to get [b]secondary products[/b] like [b]eggs[/b] or [b]milk[/b].

By using [b]Focus[/b] [b]Points[/b] you can increase the [b]chances of them producing offspring[/b] which, similar to plants, helps you to restart the process without having to spend additional Silver.

Each Royal City has a [b]local production bonus[/b] which increases the yield from [b]butchering[/b] certain animals, and of their secondary products (see table above).

[b]Riding Animals[/b]

Only Horses and Oxen can be purchased from the Farming Merchant, all other Baby Animals need to be purchased from other players or found in the wild — when killing a Wild Animal, it has a chance of dropping its corresponding Baby Animal as loot.

[b]Horses[/b], [b]Oxen[/b],[b] Stags[/b] and [b]Moose[/b] can be raised on a Pasture, while all other Riding Animals require a Kennel.

Baby Animals higher than [b]T4[/b] can also be [b]nurtured multiple times[/b], increasing the chances of them producing offspring.

When a Riding Animal is fully grown, it can be saddled at the [b]Saddler[/b] (another Farm Building which can be constructed on your island) and either used as your new riding mount or sold to other players.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/a428fea5820593da685ca95f3c97864a59767efd.jpeg[/img]

[h3]Conclusion[/h3]
Whether you choose to produce food or potions from the products of your labor, or sell them directly on the Marketplace, there are many ways you can contribute to Albion's vibrant economy — and turn a healthy profit while you do so!

Sometimes it’s a good idea to sell your products to your [b]guildmates[/b] and [b]friends[/b]. Many players are happy to buy them at a [b]small discount[/b], while both of you benefit by avoiding Marketplace taxes.

If you’re looking to [b]expand your farming space[/b] but can’t upgrade your island any further or purchase a new island in another city, you can also ask your friends or guildmates if you can use their islands. They can allow you access to their islands via the [b]Access Rights UI, [/b]and vice versa.

With this information, you should have all you need to work the land and earn your prosperity. Happy farming!

notes.title: Albion’s Horizons are Expanding!
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/6d6512b0d8a42cfd90374f633a7e10ab01235d0a.jpeg[/img]

On [b]October 28[/b], the [b]Horizons[/b] update brings new depth and excitement to Albion's open world. [b]Dynamic Encampments[/b] introduce a shifting landscape, along with [b]Dynamic Resource Hotspots[/b], new Coffers, and lair maps. Risk and reward scales by region quality in the [b]Outlands[/b], and new [b]S.A.F.E. Portals[/b] take solo players deeper within. Groups can enjoy revamped [b]Randomized Dungeons[/b] and some frightening new [b]Crystal Creatures[/b] to take down. And long-awaited quality-of-life enhancements such as the [b]HUD Editor[/b] and [b]Quick Settings Presets[/b] make your game experience smoother than ever. With two new [b]Albion Journal [/b]categories, Albion’s Horizons are expanding in many ways.

[h3]A Dynamic World[/h3]

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/8e1dd62cc6802f61d88836a8cf1e2933ee8372bc.png[/img]

[b]Dynamic Encampments[/b] are new mob camps which spawn in unpredictable locations in the open world for a limited time, offering personal rewards for those who complete them. At the same time, [b]Dynamic Resource Hotspots[/b] are springing up with abundant gathering possibilities. [b]Coffers[/b] in the open world offer rewards to those who uncover them, and new maps can sometimes be found within mob camps, which open up a special dungeon to those who are able to grab them.

[h3]Beyond the Horizon[/h3]

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/babcf7c1f788dda3839b65882d235312b8fc7ab6.png[/img]

In the [b]Outlands[/b], difficulty and rewards now scale by region quality, offering more challenging but more lucrative options as you get closer to the center. For solo players, [b]S.A.F.E. Portals[/b] provide instant travel from Portal Towns deeper into the Outlands – transporting players unpredictably into these less-trodden areas. And the [b]Crystal Beetle[/b] and [b]Crystal Cobra[/b] provide new, fearsome targets for groups. At the same time, [b]Group Randomized Dungeons[/b] have been revamped, offering greater rewards for larger teams, and on the Royal Continent [b]Tier 5 Blue Zones[/b] and [b]Tier 6 Yellow Zones[/b] offer more advanced content early in the game.

[h3]Customize Your Experience[/h3]

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/7d8c8ad95c5cd72f6f491d7f635f6c5d1c4680bd.png[/img]

The [b]HUD Editor[/b] gives you unprecedented control over your interface, allowing you to customize, save, and share layouts. Pair it with [b]Quick Settings Presets[/b] to shift between graphics, audio, controls, and gameplay settings at the touch of a button. [b]Managing your inventory[/b] is easier than ever with collapsible sections, customizable item slots, and advanced sorting options. [b]Banks [/b]also get a boost with Move All, Repair All, and more intuitive sorting features. And the [b]Albion Journal[/b] has two new categories – Social & Guild and Island – with brand-new, themed rewards.

With all this and more, Horizons opens up new opportunities in Albion’s ever-evolving world, expanding the possibilities of your experience further than ever. For more information, see this [url=https://albiononline.com/news/dev-talk-open-world-improvements][b]Dev Talk[/b][/url] on the open-world changes, and check out the official update page [url=https://albiononline.com/update/horizons][b]here[/b][/url].

notes.title: Dev Talk: Open World Improvements
notes.content:
In this Dev Talk, [b]Game Director Robin Henkys[/b] introduces [b]Horizons[/b], Albion’s next major update. This update brings new features to the Outlands, introduces more challenging PvE, and brings long-awaited quality-of-life improvements. Today, we focus on the key changes coming to the[b] open world[/b].

[previewyoutube=iCEZk_q54A0?rel=0;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3]Outlands Changes[/h3]
[b]Horizons[/b] makes the [b]Outlands[/b] more accessible and rewarding for solo and small group players, while keeping them worthy of guild conquest.

[b]S.A.F.E. Portal:[/b] [list]	[*]New [b]solo teleport system[/b] located in Portal Towns, offering instant access to random Outlands regions within a certain range[/*]	[*]The portal charges a [b]Silver fee[/b] based on weight[/*]	[*]The player can return through the portal for a limited time	[list]		[*]Certain actions, like collecting items from containers or performing trades, will cause the return portal to close[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]With their introduction, the inner-Outlands will become[b] more active and accessible[/b][/*][/list]
[b][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/7cab8d322c4cabc2eda63a9a30359ccd622c10d6.jpeg[/img][/b]

[b]Crystal Creatures:[/b][list]	[*]New creatures: [b]Crystal Beetle[/b] and [b]Crystal Cobra[/b][/*]	[*][b]Higher spawn rates[/b] for all Crystal Creatures[/*]	[*]Now [b]marked only in proximity[/b] to players[/*]	[*]Their rewards have been adjusted, but increased availability makes them a [b]reliable income option for groups[/b][/*][/list]
[b][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/1d330680ad77c1715449bafbc22391c2b55e1f5e.jpeg[/img][/b]

[b]Other Outlands Changes:[/b][list]	[*][b]Region Quality Scaling [/b]will [b]increase[/b] the rewards and difficulty of Outlands regions as you get closer to the center[/*]	[*]A new[b] Player Count Indicator[/b] shows [b]a range of active players [/b]in a particular region to help players assess PvP risk and [b]find fights[/b] of their desired scale[/*][/list]
[h3]PvE Changes and New Challenges[/h3]

[b]Dynamic Solo & Veteran Mob Camps:[/b][list]	[*][b]Camps shift location[/b] periodically and are only available for a limited time[/*]	[*]Players must earn Fame by killing mobs protecting the camp to unlock a personal [b]chest[/b][/*]	[*]They can only be cleared once, [b]encouraging open world exploration[/b][/*][/list]
[b][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/a8804422c2fdecc24532f0f61a83c91f5f9c94d4.jpeg[/img][/b]

[b]Mob Power Rebalancing:[/b][list]	[*]Mob [b]power has been adjusted,[/b] with damage and health increases from T5 (+9%) to T8 (+42%)	[list]		[*]These adjustments [b]don’t apply[/b] to:		[list]			[*]Elite enemies[/*]			[*]Avalonians[/*]			[*]Corrupted Dungeons[/*]			[*]Hellgates[/*]		[/list]		[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*] Rewards have also been[b] increased proportionally[/b] for these mobs and chests[/*][/list][b]Veteran Dungeon Rework:[/b][list]	[*]Veteran Dungeons rewards have been rebalanced to suit their [b]intended group size[/b][/*]	[*]Completing these dungeons in a group [b]grants bonus[/b] [b]rewards[/b][/*]	[*]Dungeon [b]entrances will close[/b] shortly after entry, allowing players to focus on PvE[/*][/list]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/a0058ab624d8368b8e6690f615385c01c2e64328.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Other Changes[/h3]

[b]Royal Continent Changes:[/b][list]	[*]Some T5 [b]Yellow Zones[/b] have been upgraded to [b]T6[/b], and some T4 [b]Blue Zones[/b] to [b]T5[/b][/*]	[*]T5 and T6 resource output from these regions will remain negligible in comparison to more dangerous zones[/*]	[*]This expands the content available in safe zones, without diminishing the appeal of full-loot PvP zones[/*][/list][b]Resource Hotspots:[/b][list]	[*][b]Resource Hotspots [/b]offer large amounts of resources for a limited time in random locations[/*][/list]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/18ccbc9724a4ab5d469a7d7cf1f44e1712d70de6.jpeg[/img]

Stay tuned for more Dev Talks soon, where we'll dive into the new [b]Journal categories[/b] and groundbreaking [b]QoL features[/b] coming with the [b]Horizons[/b] update!

notes.title: This Referral Season, Bring the Fun Back with the Jester Horse!
notes.content:
This October, while everyone else is riding their spooky mounts, bring some fun back to Albion with the [b]Jester Horse[/b]! [list]	[*]Refer [b]1 Friend[/b]: Jester Horse mount skin[/*]	[*]Refer [b]3 Friends[/b]: A T7 Pile of Tomes worth 100,000 Fame[/*]	[*]Refer [b]5 Friends[/b]: A T8 Pile of Tomes worth 200,000 Fame[/*]	[*]Bonus for your [b]first-ever referral[/b]: A T8 Pile of Tomes worth 200,000 Fame[/*]	[*]Additionally, for [b]each friend[/b] you refer, you'll receive [b]500 Gold[/b]![/*][/list][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/566265ea67322a7731e05b30984829f1d2036419.png[/img]

Getting your friends in on the action is as simple as following these steps:
[list]	[*][b]Step 1[/b]: Share your referral link with a friend, which you can find [url=https://albiononline.com/profile/referral/overview][b]here[/b][/url] when logged into the website with your game account.[/*]	[*][b]Step 2[/b]: Your friend signs up to Albion Online.[/*]	[*][b]Step 3[/b]: Your friend purchases at least 30 days of Premium status, unlocking your rewards.[/*][/list]Don't miss out on the chance to clown around with your pals and claim these fantastic rewards. notes.title: The Harvest Challenge Awaits
notes.content:
The[b] Harvest Challenge[/b] is here, casting long shadows over Albion as Allhallows approaches. In the darkness, the elusive [b]Spectral Bat[/b] awaits. If you’re brave enough to seek it, you can [b]unlock this ghastly mount[/b] and other haunting rewards by earning [b]Challenge Points[/b] through activities in the open world. Will you be in time to reap the harvest of shadows before the season fades into darkness?

[video autoplay="yes" loop="yes" muted="yes"]https://assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/video_/media/66fa9977f3104_720.mp4[/video]

[h3][b]Reap What You Sow[/b][/h3]
[b][img]https://assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/my-context/media/5a9e734d7a37c596bd8f341dbc3a91df18612d68.png[/img]

SPECTRAL BAT:[/b] This month's Challenge offers another chance to claim the amazing [b]Spectral Bat[/b]. In addition to its spooky appearance, this winged menace comes with a powerful [b]Flicker[/b] spell that allows you to jump to a target location in the blink of an eye. (Note: like all mounts, the Spectral Bat cannot fly over obstacles or gaps.)

[b][img]https://assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/my-context/media/19075c42b2f6083a97620356e3a682f66f0a4774.png[/img]

AVATAR RING:[/b] Adventurers who rack up enough total Challenge Points will also earn the [b]Harvest Challenge Avatar Ring[/b], featuring a pair of eerie, grinning skeletons. This non-tradable item permanently unlocks this avatar border for one character, or can be traded to the Vanity Merchant for one Vanity Token.

[b][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/2c7ba7c8b9fff4083306b993696b33ec95415878.png[/img]

SEASONAL SPECIALS:[/b] All month long, reach weekly point totals to unlock [b]Harvest Challenge Chests[/b]. Along with valuable rewards like Adventurer's Tomes, Silver, resources, and other loot, you'll also have a chance to unlock six seasonal furniture items: the [b]Scary Pumpkin Lantern, Friendly Pumpkin Lantern, Halloween Lantern, Halloween Cauldron, Halloween Scarecrow,[/b] and [b]Halloween Pyre[/b].

As always, you can earn Challenge Points by [b]gathering, fishing, farming, and killing monsters[/b]. Points count simultaneously toward a daily bonus, a weekly unlockable chest, and the monthly mount and avatar ring reward. So log in, head out into the open world, gather points, and claim these rewards while they last!

notes.title: 'Zero to Hero:' At the End of the Tour
notes.content:
[i]Join writer [/i][url=https://twitter.com/bywillborger][b][i]Will Borger[/i][/b][/url][i] in the final installment of our [b]Zero to Hero[/b] series, as he reflects on challenges faced, lessons learned, and the importance of community. (In case you missed them, catch up on parts [/i][url=https://albiononline.com/news/zero-to-hero-part-one][b][i]one[/i][/b][/url][i] and [/i][url=https://albiononline.com/news/zero-to-hero-part-two][b][i]two[/i][/b][/url][i].)[/i]

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/313f1d78ee2f158804e03ba890b7b3be76d61deb.jpeg[/img]

[h3]Zero to Hero is over, but I’m thinking of all tomorrow’s parties…[/h3]

[i]By Will Borger[/i]

Endings are hard. When I began my time with Albion Online back in April, I wasn’t thinking of how it would end, how it would feel, or what I would say when all was said and done. And as I type this final column, I’m still not sure. That’s weird for me; I don’t usually start a piece of writing until I know how I’m going to write it. I know the last line. I know what the title will be. The middle is where I get to play, but I know where the journey ends. I don’t here, but as I type this I’m beginning to see the path. And you can drive a long way with just your headlights to guide you down a dark road.

Coming into my final week, I didn’t know what the team had planned for me. I figured we’d do what we normally do: queue up, stomp some randoms, lose a couple of close games, laugh about it, and generally have a good time. I didn’t expect to play by myself. Well, Bogul came too, but I definitely didn’t expect to be on a team of randoms, and have my play judged in real time. We didn’t win — aside from Bogul, my team didn’t know what they were doing — but I played well, racking up the most damage not only on my team, but in the game. That felt good. And it was a far cry from where I’d started with the Bow, Cursed Staff, or anything else. I’d found my thing, and I was pretty good at it. I would have preferred a win, but I’ll take a personal best. It’s enough.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/94138db50c2e1f2f4b9b612b607159c347992128.jpeg[/img]

I haven’t played Albion Online since that day. Not because I don’t want to, but because the season was over and I was buried under a pile of work. I’ll be back soon. But I’ve thought about it a lot since. What follows isn’t a review of my time with Albion, but a reflection on it.

When I think of my time in Albion, I mostly remember the community. Not just Shozen, Tazzik, Lewpac, Bogul, and the others I was lucky enough to play with, but the Twitch chat, the guys we played with. Maybe they were trolling us or hyping us up, but they were there and the experience would have been worse without them.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/abd5cf038be04cbb2345363b0e2a6d50311ab152.jpeg[/img]

And that sums Albion up, when you think about it. All the gear I bought, all the stuff I learned, everyone I played against, all the advice, it all came from that community. It’s hard to build that in the gaming space these days. There’s just so much, and everything is competing with what came before. When you’re releasing a new game, you’re not just competing against another game, but you’re competing against people’s investment in that game and all of the content that’s been built up over the years. When we think about the MMO space, we think about World of Warcraft, the most popular MMO of all time, and Final Fantasy XIV, a beloved sequel to a beloved MMO in one of the most recognizable and important franchises in the history of the industry. Albion isn’t that old — it was released in 2017. But it’s carved out a space for itself. That’s damn impressive, and that speaks to Albion’s community as a whole and Sandbox Interactive’s support of it.

I think Albion’s Arena is one of the most brilliant modes of its kind that I’ve ever played. I love that it’s not just about killing the other team, but strategically capturing points at the right time. I think the decision to tie your abilities to gear and reward you for using that gear is inspired. I fell in love instantly with the way Albion works, and I’ve had more fun in the Arena and during the big 20v20s we had than in most other games, full stop. I hope that SBI will nurture and expand these modes so that they can continue to thrive. I can’t wait to get back to the Arena. Sometimes you gotta nuke people with a giant pigeon.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/e265209c87a88c8fbf93ecd1f8133ff8a60a3ed6.jpeg[/img]

I genuinely enjoyed showing up for work when I was playing Albion Online. As someone whose job is primarily to play and write about video games, trust me, that isn’t always the case. But here? I was having fun. That means something. I’ve always said that the highest compliment I can give a game is when I want to continue playing it after I’m done with it. I want to keep playing Albion Online. I can’t think of higher praise.

Remember how I started off by saying endings are hard? In this case, it’s because this isn’t really an ending. Zero to Hero is over, sure, but I’m not done yet. You’ll see me around the Arena or playing 20v20s. Nothing really ends. It just changes. The road keeps going, and you follow the headlights as long as you can. So it’s not “goodbye.” It’s “see you later.” The show ends, the curtain comes down, the house empties out, but the band plays on. And if you hear the music, you gotta dance. Thanks for coming along for the ride. I’ll see you down the road.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/9284c15e4eee2fae24cc2474f161b7896ec2a62c.jpeg[/img]

[i]A big thank you to Will for inviting us along on his journey, and to all of you who’ve followed him. But as this [b]Zero to Hero[/b] series comes to a close, new stories are being written all over Albion. So join us on our regular adventures over on [/i][url=https://www.twitch.tv/albiononline][b][i]twitch.tv/albiononline[/i][/b][/url][i]![/i]

notes.title: The Heretic Challenge Returns
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/24ff6b74ff48225c7a263ca26c68477a665167b2.jpeg[/img]

This September, plunge into the madness of the [b]Heretic Challenge[/b]. Earn points through open-world activities, unlock chests filled with the fruits of deranged craftsmanship, and claim the [b]Heretic Combat Mule[/b] – a twisted creation with a powerful cannon shot!

[h3]Mighty Mules and Heretic Decor[/h3]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/8f727a835c35856831b6572979da864effd7f0c5.png[/img]

[b]HERETIC COMBAT MULE:[/b] This month's Challenge brings back the [b]Heretic Combat Mule[/b], a war machine from the twisted minds of Heretic saddlers. The Combat Mule fires a powerful cannon shot that knocks back and slows targets, but watch out for its massive recoil!
 
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/119f51ba9c4fffc6a00b9c9f24208fc43f3b1c74.png[/img]

[b]AVATAR RING:[/b] Adventurers who rack up enough total Challenge Points will also earn the [b]Heretic Challenge Avatar Ring[/b]. This non-tradable item permanently unlocks this crazed, ramshackle avatar border for one character, or can be traded to the Vanity Merchant for one Adventurer's Token.
 
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/f100e812f7050459d2f9253296b0d5b51c54f068.png[/img]

[b]SEASONAL SPECIALS:[/b] All month long, reach weekly goals to unlock Heretic Challenge Chests. In addition to valuable rewards like Adventurer's Tomes, Silver, and resources, you'll also have a chance to unlock special furniture items like the [b]Heretic Lantern, Heretic Junkpile [/b]and [b]Heretic Scarecrow[/b].
 
[video autoplay="yes" loop="yes" muted="yes"]https://assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/video_/media/66c86d0c98bee_720.mp4[/video]

As always, you can earn Challenge Points by [b]gathering, fishing, farming, and killing monsters[/b]. Points count simultaneously toward a daily bonus, a weekly unlockable chest, and the monthly mount and avatar ring rewards. So log in, head out into the open world, gather points, and claim these rewards while they last!

notes.title: Dev Talk: August 2024 Development Update
notes.content:
We're back with another [b]Dev Talk[/b]! While everyone is busy filling out their Journals, [b]Game Director Robin Henkys[/b] sat down to unpack the key takeaways from Paths to Glory, and give you a sneak peek at what the team is cooking up next. With work on the next update well underway, there's a lot to be excited about!
 
[previewyoutube=2YLVcswGcYI;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3]After [i]Paths to Glory[/i][/h3][list]	[*]Rebalancing the [b]Roads of Avalon[/b] has led to a marked increase in both PvP and PvE activity there[/*]	[*]The next update will aim to achieve a [b]similar effect for the open world[/b][/*]	[*]The goals are:	[list]		[*]Increased attractiveness to [b]solo players[/b][/*]		[*]More rewarding [b]mid-sized group content[/b][/*]		[*]Increased [b]activity in the inner-Outlands[/b][/*]		[*]More [b]challenging and rewarding PvE[/b][/*]	[/list][/*][/list][h3][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/cde6bb5fbe0f054da69ab9f8f03c25a9e5450cb9.jpeg[/img]

[/h3]
[h3]Open World Developments[/h3][list]	[*][b]New PvE objectives[/b] for solo players[/*]	[*][b]New mechanics[/b] to help solo players journey deeper into the Outlands	[list]		[*]This will [b]reduce the risk of ganking[/b] near Portal Cities[/*]	[/list][/*]	[*]PvE rewards and difficulty in the inner-Outlands which [b]scale by region quality[/b]	[list]		[*]This should draw competition away from Portal Cities and into the [b]inner-Outlands[/b][/*]	[/list][/*]	[*]Increased rewards for group [b]Randomized Dungeons[/b][/*]	[*][b]Rebalanced mobs[/b] in the open world and Randomized Dungeons	[list]		[*]Higher-tier mobs will become more challenging and [b]more rewarding[/b][/*]		[*]This should bring [b]high-end PvE[/b] back to the open world[/*]	[/list][/*]	[*]Some [b]Tier 5 and Tier 6 content[/b] introduced to blue and yellow zones, respectively	[list]		[*]This will expand the content available to new players before entering full-loot PvP zones[/*]	[/list][/*][/list][h3][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/0ff365467a1f03cccb504661fceed8eec0b56fc0.jpeg[/img]

[/h3]
[h3]Further Improvements[/h3]
At the same time, we’re working on many other features and improvements:
[list]	[*]Two new categories in the [b]Albion Journal[/b][/*]	[*]A more [b]customizable HUD[/b][/*]	[*]Savable [b]settings presets[/b] for quick hotkey adjustments[/*]	[*][b]Inventory management[/b] improvements[/*]	[*]The next batch of [b]Crystal Weapons[/b][/*]	[*]Enhanced[b] rendering performance[/b][/*]	[*]Strengthened [b]cheat protection[/b][/*][/list][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/f84e1e63d914dd2f2647c26db7f16fcc3b9c7d99.jpeg[/img]

These developments are all part of our mission to make Albion Online the ultimate sandbox MMORPG, so stay tuned to hear more as we approach the next update. Meanwhile, if you have any questions or comments for us, check out the [b]full video[/b] and [b]leave them in the comments there[/b], and we’ll address the most popular comments in a future video!

notes.title: Celebrate International Dog Day with the Shepherd Mount Skin
notes.content:
[video autoplay="yes" loop="yes" muted="yes"]https://assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/video_/media/66ab6dfe0a5e7_720.mp4[/video]

Who's a good boy? Your Direwolf, that's who! This [b]International Dog Day[/b], give your mount the fluffiest makeover with the [b]Shepherd mount skin![/b] From [b]August 26, 2024[/b] at [b]10 UTC[/b] until [b]September 2, 2024 [/b]at [b]10 UTC[/b], you can transform your fierce friend into the cutest canine companion.

notes.title: Check out our Guide to Mounts
notes.content:
Mounts in Albion are more than just a means of transportation. Picking the right one for your adventure can even determine whether you survive an encounter or lose your hard-earned gear. In the following guide, we’ll go over some useful tips for raising, buying and riding your mounts, and show which stats and traits to look out for to make sure you aren’t easy prey out there in the wild.

[previewyoutube=nvtNMQh5EeE?si=Z3d9LULEsll3xSIG;full][/previewyoutube]
[h2]Useful Tips[/h2]
Every mount has passive stats that can help you to determine whether it’s suitable for your next adventure. These include [b]mount health[/b], [b]armor[/b], [b]magical resistance[/b], and [b]crowd control resistance,[/b] which tell you how much damage that mount can take before it throws its rider off. [b]Move[/b] and [b]gallop speed[/b], meanwhile, indicate how fast you can travel across the world: move speed refers to the basic speed of your mount, while galloping is achieved by continuously riding without taking damage.

Another important stat is [b]max load,[/b] which shows how much extra weight a mount lets you carry. Here we have to distinguish between max load, which counts as [b]active carry weight,[/b] and the ‘[b]Courier[/b]’ passive spell, which counts as [b]passive carry weight[/b].

[b]Active carry weight[/b] lets you carry more weight while riding or while you’re directly next to your mount. Being forcefully dismounted or leaving the mount radius will remove this bonus, and may leave you over-encumbered.

[b]Passive carry weight,[/b] meanwhile, increases your max load as long as you have a mount equipped, even if you’re on foot or in combat.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/deb63f7b9452830fa2b06e8e4ca861511f66d3b2.png[/img]

A number of mounts also have [b]active abilities[/b] that can be triggered while riding. Some offer abilities on the [b]shoe slot[/b] (default: F) that let you travel faster in various ways, while others have [b]weapon slot[/b] abilities (default: Q,W,E). Using an active mount ability will put that slot on [b]cooldown[/b], so if you use the shoe slot ability on your mount and then dismount, you must wait for the cooldown to end before you can use your actual shoe slot again.

Every mount has the ability ‘[b]Journey Back[/b]’ (default: R). This allows you to return to your [b]last safe zone location [/b]after a channel. This ability has a Silver cost, which is determined by the [b]distance[/b] to the nearest safe zone and the [b]items[/b] you’re carrying.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/70fa881ed4ea480485ea2d349a191b5aa1b829b1.png[/img]

When dismounted by an enemy player or creature, you become [b]immune to crowd control[/b] for a short time, while having full access to your cooldowns. You cannot remount within 30 seconds.

When dismounting voluntarily, your weapon slots are available as long as no enemy players are nearby, while your armor slots are on a [b]5 second cooldown[/b]. You will also notice a [b]circle around your mount[/b], within which you can move freely and [b]click/tap on the mount[/b] to quickly mount up again. Getting into combat with another player will immediately [b]remove[/b] the mount.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/9ba1886f55f3ea204dc8809f87f637980be21be4.png[/img]

Every mount can be traded at the Marketplace. If you decide to raise or earn a mount yourself, you will find additional information below.

[h2]The Mounts of Albion[/h2]

[h3]Starter Mounts[/h3]
When playing the tutorial, you’ll meet your very first mount - the [b]Novice’s Mule[/b]. While it isn’t the fastest, it already has the ‘Courier’ passive, granting some additional carry weight.

[b]Horses[/b] and [b]Oxen[/b] can be raised on pastures on personal islands or guild territories. Once grown, they can be saddled to become a [b]Riding Horse[/b] – an agile mount with passive carryweight – an [b]Armored Horse[/b] – a sturdy mount with additional armor for added protection – or a [b]Transport Ox[/b], which allows you to carry large quantities of goods.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/860f6f4d6d455dd8dea83ee6fba6ca50857baa6d.png[/img]

[h3]Adventurer’s Challenge Mounts[/h3]
Adventurer’s Challenge Mounts offer either [b]fast movement[/b], [b]escape abilities,[/b] or high [b]transport capacity[/b]. Each month brings a fresh challenge in which players can accumulate [b]Challenge Points[/b] to unlock daily, weekly, and monthly rewards. After completing the monthly challenge, players with active [b]Premium[/b] status can claim that month’s mount and immediately begin to use it.

Adventurer’s Challenges work on an annual rotation, with each month’s mount as follows:
[list]	[*]January: [b]Frost Ram[/b][/*]	[*]February: [b]Saddled Terrorbird[/b][/*]	[*]March: [b]Grizzly Bear[/b][/*]	[*]April: [b]Black Panther[/b][/*]	[*]May: [b]Morgana Raven[/b][/*]	[*]June: [b]Gallant Horse[/b][/*]	[*]July: [b]Spectral Direboar[/b][/*]	[*]August: [b]Divine Owl[/b][/*]	[*]September: [b]Heretic Combat Mule[/b][/*]	[*]October: [b]Spectral Bat[/b][/*]	[*]November: [b]Pest Lizard[/b][/*]	[*]December: [b]Snow Husky[/b][/*][/list]

[video autoplay="yes" loop="yes" muted="yes"]https://assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/video_/media/665ed6c360391_720.mp4[/video]

[h3]Rare Baby Animals[/h3]
Some baby animals can be acquired by [b]killing open world hide animals[/b]. These can then be raised on a pasture or in a kennel.

The chances of one of these baby animals dropping [b]decreases with the tier of the mob[/b].

You have a chance of finding each type of baby animal in the following biomes:
[list]	[*][b]Steppe:[/b] Stag (T4) / Swiftclaw (T5) / Mammoth (T8)[/*]	[*][b]Forest: [/b]Direwolf (T6) / Moose (T6) / Direboar (T7) / Direbear (T8)[/*]	[*][b]Swamp:[/b] Swamp Salamander (T6) / Direboar (T7) / Direbear (T8)[/*][/list]
There is also a small chance that [b]Conqueror’s Chests[/b] contain one of these.

[b]Swiftclaws[/b] and [b]Direwolves[/b] are very quick, while others, like the [b]Moose,[/b] are great at carrying medium loads while remaining agile. The [b]Transport Mammoth[/b] is by far the best mount for carrying a lot of weight.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/a1dc4bfce579f162edf69cc39a2d7cffed8318ea.png[/img]

[h3]Faction Mounts[/h3]
Each major city in Albion hosts a faction that players can fight for to earn [b]Faction Points[/b]. These points can be used to acquire baby animals. Each city has a [b]standard[/b] and an [b]elite version[/b] of their mount to choose from.

In addition to the six Royal Cities, [b]Brecilien[/b] also offers two baby animals that can be purchased with [b]Favor[/b].

Each city’s mounts are:
[list]	[*]Thetford: [b]Swamp Salamander[/b] & [b]Elite Swamp Salamander[/b][/*]	[*]Fort Sterling: [b]Winter Bear[/b] & [b]Elite Winter Bear[/b][/*]	[*]Lymhurst: [b]Wild Boar[/b] & [b]Elite Wild Boar[/b][/*]	[*]Bridgewatch: [b]Terrorbird[/b] & [b]Elite Terrorbird[/b][/*]	[*]Martlock: [b]Bighorn Ram[/b] & [b]Elite Bighorn Ram[/b][/*]	[*]Caerleon: [b]Greywolf[/b] & [b]Elite Greywolf[/b][/*]	[*]Brecilien: [b]Mystic Owl[/b] & [b]Elite Mystic Owl[/b][/*][/list]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/b9907d7385b04059f626f88150783f6dcf48a103.jpeg[/img]

[h3]Battle Mounts[/h3]
Battle mounts are used in [b]large-scale battles[/b] to enhance the survivability and offensive strength of a zerg. They can offer [b]buffs[/b] to big groups of players and shape the battlefield with their [b]disruptive skills[/b]. These mounts are usually tough to take down.

Most battle mounts are given out at the end of a [b]Guild Season[/b] through [b]Conqueror’s Chests[/b]. Attaining a higher [b]guild rank[/b] and a better chest [b]increases the chances[/b] of getting battle mounts. Players engaging in high-level [b]20v20 Crystal League[/b] matches also have a chance to receive these.

Some battle mounts can only be obtained through the [b]Energy Manipulator[/b]. They require a base mount, some [b]materials,[/b] and a large amount of [b]Siphoned Energy[/b].

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/e422e5c7f96d451dfaa7969508e78308c2dab65e.png[/img]

[h3]Special Mounts[/h3]
There are also a few rare mounts that don’t fall into any of the above categories, like the [b]Morgana Nightmare[/b], the [b]Rageclaw,[/b] and the [b]Spectral Bonehorse[/b]. Each of these can be crafted from artifacts dropped by [b]World Bosses[/b] found in special raid zones in the open world.

The [b]Rites of Spring[/b] event allows players to earn the [b]Spring Cottontail[/b] and [b]Caerleon Cottontail[/b] mounts.

Some older referral seasons rewarded unique mounts.

And, last but not least, the [b]Avalonian Basilisk[/b] can be acquired with a Saddled Swamp Dragon and 5000 Avalonian Energy at the Saddler.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/a689aee5cd2405abf12587751d47c486ecd097ab.png[/img]

[h2]Mount Skins[/h2]
[b]You are what you wear[/b]. So make yourself a dashing adventurer or a gruesome warrior while you’re riding through Albion! There are a multitude of skins available to give your favorite mount a makeover - simply go to the [b]Appearance[/b] [b]UI[/b] in the player menu to check out which skins are available.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/205cc0aa8ca695bf2198b053e3143cf204980f30.jpeg[/img]

Many skins can be purchased from the [url=https://albiononline.com/shop/vanity][b]Albion Online Web Shop[/b][/url] or ingame store[b],[/b] while some can be purchased for [b]Gold[/b] or earned by [url=https://albiononline.com/profile/referral/overview][b]referring a friend[/b][/url]. Referral mount skins can be traded at the Marketplace.

Ready to ride? With this knowledge you'll be well-equipped to traverse Albion's treacherous roads with the right mount for any occasion. Giddy up!

notes.title: ‘Zero to Hero’: The Bird is the Word
notes.content:
[i]This series follows writer [/i][url=https://twitter.com/bywillborger][b][i]Will Borger[/i][/b][/url][i] as he joins the [/i][url=https://www.twitch.tv/albiononline][b][i]AlbionTV[/i][/b][/url][i] crew on his very own Path to Glory. In this, the second installment, he finds his calling in an unfamiliar weapon. (Read part one [/i][url=https://albiononline.com/news/zero-to-hero-part-one][b][i]here[/i][/b][/url][i].)[/i]

[i]By Will Borger[/i]

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/aaf6efd8fd29131b98f7eb3feca6fb7337173d2a.jpeg[/img]

Everything clicked once I could start dropping nukes.

I wrapped my last Zero to Hero a couple of days ago, and I’m still thinking about the journey. But that’s not the subject of this write-up. You’ll hear from me one more time in a couple weeks, after the whole thing has marinated a bit. Right now, dear readers, I’d like to catch you up on what’s happened since you last heard from me in… May. Whoops. Time and tide, and all that.

Last time on Zero to Hero, we were at rock bottom. We were losing a lot, I didn’t know what I was doing, we were trying to find the right build… It was a lot. But as I said in May, I didn’t expect to stay at rock bottom forever.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/89fcfa072ad6ec6d12d5d57350b0c94db141acce.jpeg[/img]

Sometimes, the fix you need comes from somewhere you don’t expect. In this case, though, it was someone. I had no shortage of expert advice - I was playing with Lewpac, Bogul, Shozen, and Tazzik, after all - but the suggestion that changed my ever-lovin’ Albion life came from Meletriss, who, after one show was over, suggested I try out Lightcaller. I had no idea what a Lightcaller was, but I did know that Great Curse staff wasn’t working for me. As the old saying goes, I’ll try anything once.

When I play a game, one of two things tends to happen: I either find my character/class/weapon almost immediately and stick with it forever, or I fumble around for a while until something clicks. With Albion, there was a lot of fumbling. We started with a Longbow, moved to a regular Bow, tried out the Great Curse Staff, and, eventually, settled on the Lightcaller. But I never would have gotten there without Meletriss. We only spoke a few times during my run on AlbionTV, but she changed the trajectory of the show with one simple suggestion. Funny how that works out. Thanks, Mel.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/8cbf6f6eadf63ad678ad0f9cf908939d72565a3e.jpeg[/img]

Lightcaller wasn’t a plug-in and play, either. The early games were… rough. You wanna see someone do 10,000 damage on a Lightcaller? Watch my early games. I wasn’t managing my stacks well, using my auto-attacks to set up my Q, switching at the right times, landing my Ws, you name it. You want a primer on how not to play Lightcaller? Watch my first few games.

But it’s amazing what a couple of examples can do. One day, after he was tired of me doing less damage on Lightcaller than his cat did while walking across his keyboard, Lewpac had me watch him play a couple games with the Lightcaller. We went over positioning, using the auto-attacks to set up the Q, when to switch, using defensives, and so much more. And seeing it in action, I finally understood.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/9a391bb174dc4bcfcbad5b0d021cf1a182601d24.jpeg[/img]

I’ve said it before: I’m a fighting game player, and playing that genre taught me how I improve: practice. I’m decent at games when I first pick them up, but if I actually want to improve, I have to put in the time, watch replays, see what the pros do, and so on. I have a lot of respect for people who can pick something up and immediately be good at it. But that’s never been me.

Bird had the thing all the other things I’d tried since the Bow had lacked: it was fun. So I knew what I needed to do. Stick with the bird.

And slowly but surely, the numbers started to go up. 15,000 damage. Then 20,000. And by the time my last show happened, 30,000, pretty reliably. That’s a story for the final piece, though.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/a900fc887db647c85f1cf9070a47e9615d59feb8.jpeg[/img]

Picking one build and sticking with it unlocked Albion’s arena for me. Once I knew and liked what I was doing each game, it became easier to form a stable gameplan, and once I had that, I had to think less about what I needed to be doing, and more about what the other team was doing, and how I could coordinate with my team to beat it.

I’ll stop there for now. I want to save some stuff for a couple weeks from now, and I want to spend a little more time in Albion before I give my final thoughts. But in my experience, every competitive game has the one thing that unlocks it for you, whether it’s a weapon, character, class, or something else entirely. For me, it was the Lightcaller Staff. And that’s when I finally understood Albion, and when everything started to click. All hail the pigeon.

[i]Stay tuned for the final piece in this series, and watch Will’s journey unfold live on [/i][url=https://www.twitch.tv/albiononline][b][i]AlbionTV[/i][/b][/url][i] every Saturday at 19 UTC![/i]

notes.title: Guild Season 23 Wrapup
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/d9b6e3c4753e67b55cedbbba7b146e86b84fb4da.jpeg[/img]

With the dust having settled on another intense [b]Guild Season[/b], it’s time to take a look at the fierce battles that took place and the ever-shifting landscape of Albion’s alliances. With the first full season on Albion Europe, and old rivalries reigniting elsewhere, the struggle for power has never been more thrilling. Read on to find out how [b]Sex and Flex[/b], [b]PLAC[/b], and [b]IFures[/b], secured their victories:

[h3]Albion Europe: Sex and Flex wins the server’s inaugural season[/h3]
A brand new server means new guilds, alliances, and coalitions going to war to control the Outlands and make their mark on the world of Albion.

In the beginning, we saw battles raging with fighters in modest T4 gear, riding their Mules into battle like true warriors. But it didn't take long for the players to get stronger and the gear bumped up to T8 – then those poor Mules were no more.

Soon, the first coalition war broke out on the European server. [b]Sex and Flex[/b], in an attempt to push for the first season victory, formed a massive coalition to support their efforts. The winners of the [url=https://albiononline.com/news/europe-beta-season-winners][b]Albion Europe Beta Season[/b][/url], [b]Escalation[/b], led the fightback, with their eyes also on the title. Massive battles took place day after day across multiple time slots. Escalation really had their work cut out for them, as the Sex and Flex coalition was also extremely large. They were not alone, however, as [b]Woof Woof[/b] was there to support them, and [b]PLAC[/b] was also summoned from the Asia server to lend a hand.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/8165c37c87a1d5ae0d7761f18ae4977ba400a104.jpeg[/img]

But it wasn't to be. With internal drama, and Del having no time to lead, Escalation was unable to sustain the charge, and within a month or so of the Albion Europe launch, they effectively folded. This allowed Sex and Flex to push on unchallenged and take the server’s first ever season title.

[b]Smurfing Monkeys[/b] has opened the season with a strong showing, but couldn't hold off the forces of [b]Vodafone[/b], with [b]BOBER[/b] also wreaking havoc on them in the final month. All of this damage caused the guild to close its doors after one last run at second place.

[b]APE[/b] was able to place third, resulting in all three members of the same coalition taking the top three spots.

[b]Top 10 Guilds[/b]:
[olist]	[*][b]Sex and Flex[/b] (970,117 points)[/*]	[*][b]Smurfing Monkeys[/b] (734,820 points)[/*]	[*][b]APE[/b] (536,057 points)[/*]	[*][b]Pro Bono[/b] (474,950 points)[/*]	[*][b]POLSKA GUROM[/b] (463,401 points)[/*]	[*][b]Quackers[/b] (403,712 points)[/*]	[*][b]AURORA[/b] (399,055 points)[/*]	[*][b]Vodafone[/b] (395,372 points)[/*]	[*][b]CONTROL[/b] (388,435 points)[/*]	[*][b]Escalation[/b] (382,503 points)[/*][/olist][h3]Albion Asia: PLAC remains uncontested[/h3]
Season 23 started out the same as Season 22, with [b]PLAC[/b] claiming that they were going to push for the season title. And with a strong coalition still in place, there wasn't much standing in their way.

However, a handful of guilds tried to stop them. [b]Radiant[/b] and their coalition attempted to fight back, but after a few short weeks, with well over a thousand players involved at once, it was too much for them to handle. Henrie, the guild master of Radiant, called it a day to refocus their efforts on the European server.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/b040461634e16e8073c179bd048bcc7e080237c7.jpeg[/img]

Weeks passed, and PLAC managed to hold onto the #1 spot for the entire season, taking home their third Crystal Gem with astounding back-to-back season victories, making them only the second guild in Albion’s history to do so.

In spite of that, shot caller [b]Fuckcall[/b] parted ways with PLAC at the end of the season and announced that they will attempt to lead [b]Peony Flower[/b] to victory in Season 24. But it won't be plain sailing, as the [b]Arthur's Rest[/b] coalition has formed and is already pushing back against PLAC's major holdings in territory ownership and Hideout placement. Season 24 is already shaping up to be a very interesting one for Albion Asia! 

[b]Top 10 Guilds[/b]:
[olist]	[*][b]PLAC[/b] (865,973 points)[/*]	[*][b]Kestrel[/b] (795,387 points)[/*]	[*][b]V U A[/b] (753,591 points)[/*]	[*][b]Agila[/b] (691,827 points)[/*]	[*][b]KORAWA[/b] (506,869 points)[/*]	[*][b]TUK TUK[/b] (478,948 points)[/*]	[*][b]Minerva-X[/b] (324,514 points)[/*]	[*][b]I The Flying Dutchman I[/b] (320,096 points)[/*]	[*][b]Candy Kingdom[/b] (317,297 points)[/*]	[*][b]Arirang[/b] (297,031 points)[/*][/olist][h3]Albion Americas: IFures secures a second crown[/h3]
Season 23's Outland wars picked up where Season 22 left off, with little change to the overall landscape. The [b]IFures[/b] coalition held strong, but the [b]BOBER[/b] alliance wasn't going down without a fight, and battles raged throughout the season as IFures sought their second season victory.

[b]The Lonely Men [/b]looked extremely healthy throughout, and held onto second place with the help of [b]FAX[/b]. But one thing was missing: the POE alliance withdrew after some drama unfolded, and a once mighty force in the Outlands slowly faded from the war. At the end of the season, the oldest Hideout in Albion was destroyed for the first time. Owned by the leader of the POE Alliance, [b]Crimson Imperium Reborn[/b], its fall marks the end of a legacy seen only once in the world of Albion Online…

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/9114df1d0b71ad641962aafacc9668685c2f2e75.jpeg[/img]

Coming back to the race for the crown, it looked like it would be an easy second place for The Lonely Men, but with the final Invasion Day of the season and all territories' payouts happening, a plan was hatched by the IFures coalition to have [b]PIVAS[/b], one of their members, take second place.

And so, on the final day, battles took place. But it wasn't just about fighting, and Silver payments were made to guilds all over the Outlands so that PIVAS could get their territories for their stored Season Points. With this plan in place, PIVAS was able to grab a total of 60 territories and, gaining over 200,000 Season Points, leapfrog over The Lonely Men to take second place.

[b]Top 10 Guilds[/b]:
[olist]	[*][b]IFures[/b] (907,399 points)[/*]	[*][b]PIVAS[/b] (900,298 points)[/*]	[*][b]The Lonely Men[/b] (799,138 points)[/*]	[*][b]I Guess What I[/b] (500,362 points)[/*]	[*][b]Outlimits[/b] (453,720 points)[/*]	[*][b]Pressur3[/b] (420,880 points)[/*]	[*][b]Fax[/b] (412,510 points)[/*]	[*][b]Mono Con Navaja[/b] (356,959 points)[/*]	[*][b]D R U Y D S[/b] (310,002 points)[/*]	[*][b]I M O R T A I S[/b] (305,877 points)[/*][/olist][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/4cc727135faacdf65f74bfa8fd2668ab7e34b85e.jpeg[/img]

Season 23 will be remembered for its intense battles and guild-breaking drama across Europe, Asia, and the Americas. With [b]Season 24[/b] underway, new challenges and alliances are forming, setting the stage for another thrilling chapter in Albion’s history. Adventurers are invited to check the full season schedule on our [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/199541-Season-24-Schedules/][b]forum post[/b][/url] and prepare for the exciting battles ahead!
