notes.title: Dev Talk: 2024 Update Plan
notes.content:
With[b] [url=https://albiononline.com/update/wild-blood]Wild Blood[/url][/b] having expanded Albion’s gameplay significantly, it’s already time to look forward to what the future will bring for the game. In this new Dev Talk, [b]Game Director Robin Henkys [/b]shares some of our thoughts and impressions about the update, and what that means for Albion going forward.

[previewyoutube=PMjlJSQljWM?rel=0;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3]The Wild Blood Update[/h3]
Wild Blood took longer than most updates to produce, for a number of reasons:
[list]	[*]The launch of [b]Albion East[/b], and the various challenges this presented[/*]	[*]Multiple [b]groundbreaking features[/b]	[list]		[*][b]Shapeshifter Weapons[/b] work differently to any previous weapon line[/*]		[*][b]Awakened Weapons[/b] added new stats to the combat system[/*]		[*][b]Tracking[/b] brought new quest and spawning systems to the open world[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Working on [b]many features in parallel [/b]means they slow each other down somewhat[/*][/list]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/237152502d2a714f4b9358697588cbae08a650da.jpeg[/img]
[h3]New Update Cycle[/h3]
With this in mind, we’re looking at ways to get updates out more quickly and reliably:
[list]	[*]Updates will be tied to the Guild Season schedule, coming roughly [b]every three months[/b][/*]	[*]Updates will be smaller, and targeted at a [b]specific area of the game[/b][/*]	[*]Other changes being worked on can be released [b]as and when they are ready[/b][/*][/list]
Updates will therefore vary in size depending on how many features are completed in each cycle, and the next update will never be far off. This way we can focus on the key features of each, ensuring they are delivered to the highest possible standard.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/4788cb5355c987e0f913cc2db05819fec2ce6584.jpeg[/img]
[h3]The Next Update[/h3]
Our first update on the new schedule will release in January:
[list]	[*]It will focus on [b]Guild Seasons[/b][/*]	[*]It will feature a [b]new line of rewards[/b], which expands every season	[list]		[*]These can be earned by helping your guild climb the season rankings[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]The way [b]territories [/b]produce Season Points will be reworked[/*]	[*]A new territory [b]raiding mechanic [/b]will drive conflict between guilds[/*]	[*]Individual players will be rewarded with a [b]daily Might bonus [/b]for successful territory control and raiding[/*][/list]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/b81566b502b08ce449a6d6d076b6fe017ed1249b.jpeg[/img]

Additionally, there will be various tweaks and rebalancing, including revisiting [b]Hideouts and Headquarter Hideouts[/b], to increase competition for Power Cores.

We’ll have more information for you as we approach January’s release date, so stay tuned for more!

notes.title: Guide: Tracking
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/2b4ec16eceaa7d040758f0bb4d0c5a2d3d4c5d54.jpeg[/img]

Tracking is a new open world activity that sends you and your group out into the open world to pursue rare creatures.
[h3]Tracking 101[/h3]
To begin Tracking, you’ll first need to unlock the Trainee Tracker node on the Destiny Board, which you can do by getting a small amount of PvE fame. This will allow you to use T3 tracking toolkits. These can either be crafted at a Toolmaker, or purchased directly from the Marketplace.

There are a total of seven types of creatures that you can encounter, each coming in a small version for 1-3 players, and a larger version for 4-8 players. Hunting in a party bigger than these designated sizes is not possible.
[h3]Starting the Hunt[/h3]
To initiate the hunt, you will first need to enter a red or black zone. You can then use the Tracking Toolkit either by clicking on it in your inventory, or with a hotkey (default: U).

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/c9040238fd3cbe91924901fbcbf5b7e63eeef288.jpeg[/img]

This will reveal any readable tracks in your vicinity. A T3 tool can reveal Panthers, Sylvians, and Spirit Bears, with each tier after that adding one more type of creature. Higher tier Toolkits also increase the radius in which you can discover new tracks. Go to one of the tracks you have revealed and interact with it to start the hunt.

Now you will be directed to a specific area to search for further clues. This can be within the same map, but could also lead you to a neighboring zone. Search the marked area, and you will either discover tracks or the creature itself.
[h3]Finding and Interacting with Tracks[/h3]
When you find your target’s tracks, you will need to interact with them in order to progress the hunt. The tracks will be surrounded by a small circle and may have some mobs around them protecting it. You’ll first need to clear these mobs before you can interact with the track.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/4b5a227a3701fcfa3989bddc9c6d178c932ee435.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Engaging the Target[/h3]
If you find the target itself you will need to fight it in order to progress. You may not be able to kill it on your first encounter, as the creature may flee after receiving a certain amount of damage, after a time limit has been reached, or if too many players are nearby.

But don’t worry, any damage you’ve dealt to it will carry over to the next encounter. If you end up killing the target it will drop various items, ranging from rare ingredients that can be used to craft potions, to powerful artifacts which are necessary to craft the new Shapeshifter Weapons.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/f542ac634595d8df925c19b9cb818228ebeb3d3c.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Rewards[/h3]
Any step of the hunt after its initiation will award Tracking Fame to you and your party members if you have a Tracking Toolkit in your inventory. Tracking Fame progresses the Seasoned Tracker node on the Destiny Board and its related specializations. This allows you to use better Tracking Toolkits and hunt more efficiently.

Each creature can drop new items which can be used for crafting and enchanting:
[list]	[*][b]Animal remains:[/b] Enchanting Potions[/*]	[*][b]Rare Ingredients:[/b] New Potions and Shapeshifter Weapons[/*]	[*][b]Artifacts:[/b] Artifact Shapeshifter Weapons[/*][/list]
Note: for the first few months after the Wild Blood launch, more tracks will spawn for small groups. These additional tracks will drop Black Market loot instead of rare ingredients and artifacts.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/be28e216995071f26e8ae4303141204bcc3c04e9.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Different Tiers of Tracking Toolkits and Specialization[/h3]
Unlocking and using better Tracking Toolkits has many advantages. Not only does it allow you to track higher rarity creatures, it also rewards more Fame, speeds up interactions with tracks, and increases the search radius in which you can find new tracks.

Here’s an overview of the types of creatures that can be found and interacted with, as well as the Fame bonus you receive, depending on the tier of your toolkit.
[table]			[tr]			[td]			
[b]Tracking Toolkit[/b]
			[/td]			[td]			
[b]Creature Unlocked[/b]
			[/td]			[td]			
[b]Bonus Fame[/b]
			[/td]		[/tr]		[tr]			[td]			
[b]T3[/b]
			[/td]			[td]			
Panthers
			
Sylvians
			
Spirit Bears
			[/td]			[td]			
-
			[/td]		[/tr]		[tr]			[td]			
[b]T4[/b]
			[/td]			[td]			
Werewolf
			[/td]			[td]			
5%
			[/td]		[/tr]		[tr]			[td]			
[b]T5[/b]
			[/td]			[td]			
Hellfire Imp
			[/td]			[td]			
10%
			[/td]		[/tr]		[tr]			[td]			
[b]T6[/b]
			[/td]			[td]			
Runestone Golem
			[/td]			[td]			
15%
			[/td]		[/tr]		[tr]			[td]			
[b]T7[/b]
			[/td]			[td]

			[/td]			[td]

			[/td]		[/tr]		[tr]			[td]

			[/td]			[td]

			[/td]			[td]			
30%
			[/td]		[/tr]	[/table]
In addition to better Toolkits, you can also increase your specialization in tracking each type of creature. This will further boost your Tracking Efficiency as well as increasing your chances of encountering your target at each stage rather than another track.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/822a7388c59ad340394fce4f206b57a446e3c325.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Tracking in a Party[/h3]
The size of your party matters. Not only does each creature come in two different difficulty levels offering different rewards, there’s also a benefit to hunting a rare creature that you may not be able to track down yourself yet.
[list]	[*]Small creatures for 1-3 players are easier to kill but offer lower rewards when killed. The Tracking Fame given is the same no matter whether you’re solo or in a group, but rewards will be shared between all party members.[/*]	[*]Large creatures for 4-8 players are much harder to kill and offer a higher chance of rare ingredient and artifact drops.[/*][/list]
Additionally, the more party members interact with a track, the faster the interaction will channel. During this process, the interaction speed bonuses of each member are added together.

When starting a new hunt, you want the member with the highest specialization to interact with the track, as it will use their specialization levels for the entire hunt. Even if you don’t interact with a track, as long as you’re carrying a Tracking Toolkit you will earn Tracking Fame and progress your Destiny Board.

notes.title: Get the Heretic Warsteed this Referral Season
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/516e970c53d9b166d5f02d3e80b1d51eaf97e820.jpeg[/img]

The battlefield is a wasteland. All around, the earth is parched and littered with hundreds of trashed, useless weapons. Rats pick at what they can before scuttling away into the shadows. For a second, it seems like all life has ceased. Then the smoke clears, the earth shakes, and across the carnage steps the meanest, scariest pony you’ve ever seen in your life.

It’s the [b]Heretic Warsteed[/b], and you can claim this nightmarish nag this month with just a single referral. With armor fashioned from thick slabs of scavenged wood, coarse leather strewn across its back, and a candle stuck to its head, this will be the last sight your enemies want to see coming towards them - and for many, it will be the last. The Heretic Warsteed can be used on your [b]Armored Horse [/b]base mount and, once unlocked, can be used by any characters on that particular server (either [b]Albion East[/b] or [b]West[/b]).

notes.title: Wild Blood is Here
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/4a91f641db303448452681256a7f5250b0fc9a45.jpeg[/img]

[b]Wild Blood[/b] is now live! This update introduces some major new additions and improvements to Albion’s gameworld, with [b]Shapeshifter Weapons[/b], [b]Tracking[/b], [b]Awakened Weapons[/b], new and reworked [b]potions[/b], and much more.

To mark the update, we’ve produced a new trailer:
[previewyoutube=fXc7B8_mrx8;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3]Fearsome New Forms[/h3]
[b]Shapeshifter Weapons [/b]are a brand-new Staff weapon line which allow players to transform into fantastical beasts mid-combat, expanding the possibilities of combat builds and bringing a new level to Albion’s ‘you are what you wear’ system. [b]Tracking[/b], meanwhile, is a new activity in which these same creatures can be hunted across the open world by groups. These hunts will take you along unexpected paths, but success can reward you with rare, magical artifacts and ingredients.

[h3]New Powers Unleashed[/h3]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/1924b67c0898887f9a0c132c9b7460a3fb94b24b.jpeg[/img]

The ingredients gained through Tracking can be used to craft [b]seven powerful new potions[/b] and Shapeshifter Artifact Weapons, while potions can now be enchanted to new levels. Meanwhile, [b]Awakened Weapons [/b]can be attuned with unique combinations of traits, allowing the bearer to wield immense strength. These weapons may be lost in combat, of course, but their traits will live on, telling their story and that of their owners.

[h3]Additional Improvements[/h3]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/7ec2347c20c2db1e4ba9ad6ccaa6d77104c36879.jpeg[/img]

[b]Personal Islands[/b] now have stunning new visuals, reflecting the biome of the city they are attached to, and players can now own more than one island. Furthermore, new farming bonuses for each of these biomes encourage trade across Albion and economic specialization. [b]Randomized Dungeons [/b]have expressive new visuals too, along with reworked layouts and some colossal new enemies you may encounter. And the [b]Death Recap [/b]lets players go over their recent combat defeats, to hone their skills before returning to the fray.

[h3]Celebrate Wild Blood with Twitch Drops[/h3]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/98eba5eddd577bcafb377bca36e5dc4d3a0be8d1.jpeg[/img]

To mark the release of Wild Blood, we’re running a special [b]Twitch Drops[/b] campaign in addition to our regular campaign! For full details, see [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/187153][b]this forum post[/b][/url].

For the complete list of changes coming with this update, see the [url=https://albiononline.com/changelog/wild-blood-update][b]patchnotes[/b][/url], and for more info, check out the [url=https://albiononline.com/update/wild-blood][b]official update page[/b][/url].

notes.title: Dev Talk: Shapeshifter Close-Up
notes.content:
The [url=https://albiononline.com/update/wild-blood][b]Wild Blood[/b][/url] update launches [b]October 16[/b], and at its heart is a brand-new weapon line: [b]Shapeshifter Weapons[/b]. In this Dev Talk, Game Director Robin Henkys and Combat Designer Michael Schwahn take an in-depth look at this significant expansion to Albion’s ‘you are what you wear’ system.

[previewyoutube=6hs6LuSipEw;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3]A New Staff Line[/h3]
Shapeshifter Weapons introduce a whole new style of gameplay:
[list]	[*]There are [b]seven different staffs[/b][/*]	[*]Each lets you transform into a different creature, known as [b]Shapes[/b][/*]	[*]Each Shape has its own [b]abilities and stats[/b], from damage dealer to tank[/*][/list]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/dbfe4adb52fc25f884f6db000226af19327ff6b1.jpeg[/img]

When in human form:
[list]	[*]Shapeshifter Weapons can [b]inflict damage, disrupt enemies, or support allies[/b][/*]	[*]They can also transform enemies into [b]weak, helpless creatures[/b][/*]	[*]Using human-form abilities builds up [b]Shift Charges[/b], which provide energy to Shape-form abilities[/*][/list][h3]Shapes and Abilities[/h3]
These are the different Shapes into which you can transform:
[list]	[*][b]Shadow Panther[/b]: turns invisible when no enemies are nearby[/*]	[*][b]Sylvian[/b]: increases allies’ health, provides healing, and can create a shield for your allies[/*]	[*][b]Spirit Bear[/b]: an aggressive tank that disrupts enemies[/*]	[*][b]Werewolf[/b]: Heals itself and gains a speed boost from attacking enemies[/*]	[*][b]Hellfire Imp[/b]: Has very high damage but low defense; can revive in human form after death[/*]	[*][b]Runestone Golem[/b]: a huge tank which is immune to all forced movement[/*]	[*][b]Dawnbird[/b]: deals very high damage from a safe distance[/*][/list]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/29ab7ea371f96467be99815300907d747b04f392.jpeg[/img]

These Shapes offer a wide variety of playstyles:
[list]	[*]They [b]completely override your human armor stats[/b], allowing you to change roles mid-combat	[list]		[*]For example, a Prowling Staff with Plate Armor makes you a tank in human form and an assassin in Shape form[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Previously active buffs continue in Shape form	[list]		[*]For example, you can use a Hunter Jacket then transform into a Werewolf to utilize the auto-attack buff[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Toggle and Channel abilities do not carry over[/*][/list]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/98c918e58d41ebc43616cad3e98f5818b6efe91d.jpeg[/img]

Awareness of when to transform is crucial to using these weapons. This creates an active and enjoyable playstyle that is quick to pick up but offers a great deal of depth.
[h3]How to Get Them[/h3]
Shapeshifter Weapons:
[list]	[*]Are crafted at the Hunter’s Lodge[/*]	[*]Require rare ingredients dropped by the corresponding creature in the open world[/*]	[*]These can be found using Tracking Kits[/*][/list]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/884cb028260b218e0b2bb894aa52d0318c4cc413.jpeg[/img]

Thus, Shapeshifter Weapons should remain quite rare and valuable, and bolster the appeal of [url=https://albiononline.com/news/dev-talk-tracking-potions][b]Tracking[/b][/url].

Begin your hunt for a Shapeshifter Weapon when Wild Blood launches on October 16! Which will you pick?

notes.title: Dev Talk: Tracking and Potions
notes.content:
[url=https://albiononline.com/update/wild-blood][b]Wild Blood[/b][/url] is nearby, and you’ll be able to hunt some down for yourself when the update launches. In this Dev Talk, Game Director Robin Henkys looks at [b]Tracking[/b], a new feature where you pursue creatures across the open world.

[previewyoutube=chbbRlKZ;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3]Finding Tracks[/h3]
The tracks of rare creatures can be found in the [b]Outlands [/b]and in [b]Red Zones [/b]of the Royal Continent. To interact with these, players need a [b]Tracking Toolkit[/b]. These are craftable at the [b]Toolmaker[/b] and can be used by:
[list]	[*]Clicking on a track[/*]	[*]Using from inventory	[list]		[*]This reveals nearby tracks on the map[/*]		[*]Higher tier Tracking Toolkits reveal tracks in a wider area[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/1e21d6a1a934daafff4694d3e3554c7a0ccb2c43.jpeg[/img]

There are [b]seven types of creature [/b]you can Track, each of which exists in [b]two sizes[/b]:
[list]	[*]A smaller one, for [b]up to three players[/b][/*]	[*]A larger one, for [b]four-to-eight players[/b][/*][/list]
If your party is too big or small the track, you won’t be able to follow it.

The [b]first tracks [/b]that players can find are those of [b]Panthers[/b], [b]Sylvians[/b], and [b]Spirit Bears[/b]. Rarer creatures require higher-level tracking skills and higher-tier Tracking Kits.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/25528d01a80acfe776a07b89b58a569b314e42a6.jpeg[/img]
[h3]On the Prowl[/h3]
After a track is successfully read, the hunt begins:
[list]	[*]Players are [b]guided to an area[/b][/*]	[*]Once you reach that area, you will have to [b]search for further tracks or the target itself[/b][/*]	[*]Party members can collaborate to [b]read tracks more quickly[/b][/*]	[*]Each completed step rewards [b]Tracking Fame [/b]to all party members, which boosts your Tracking skill[/*]	[*]The chances of encountering the target at each step increases with:	[list]		[*]The [b]number of steps [/b]already completed[/*]		[*]Your [b]Tracking skill[/b][/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/54240209f9c29cd20bcce5a884f26875fdcbaa22.jpeg[/img][/b]

When you encounter your target, a fight ensues. But the creature may flee if:
[list]	[*]Its [b]health [/b]falls too low[/*]	[*]The fight lasts [b]too long[/b][/*]	[*][b]Too many players [/b]attack[/*][/list]
A target that flees will have to be tracked to its new location, but any damage it has taken remains.
[h3]Spoils of the Hunt[/h3]
A defeated creature can drop various new items which are used for the following:
[list]	[*][b]Rare Animal Remains[/b]: enchanting Potions[/*]	[*][b]Rare Ingredients[/b]: crafting new Potions and Shapeshifter Weapons[/*]	[*][b]Artifacts[/b]: crafting Artifact Shapeshifter Weapons[/*][/list]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/de3339c62adcd4e914172e55a148e33981cf6bce.jpeg[/img]

These are the new Potions:
[list]	[*][b]Calming Potion[/b]: from Shadowpanther Claws, provides a PvE disengage[/*]	[*][b]Cleansing Potion[/b]: from Sylvian Roots, cleanses damage over time, crowd control, and debuffs[/*]	[*][b]Acid Potion[/b]: from Spirit Bear Paws, decreases resistances[/*]	[*][b]Berserk Potion[/b]: from Werewolf Fangs, boosts damage but decreases your defense[/*]	[*][b]Hellfire Potion[/b]: from Imp Horns, deals damage-over-time[/*]	[*][b]Gathering Potion[/b]: from Runestone Golem Teeth, increases gathering speed[/*]	[*][b]Tornado Potion[/b]: from Dawnbird Feathers, knocks enemies back[/*][/list]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/7a7aa94533cb34b00f78fe9225bc3f06dd3c3035.jpeg[/img]

Rare Animal Remains can be reduced to [b]Arcane Extract[/b], to enchant Potions:
[list]	[*]Potions now have [b]three levels of enchantment[/b][/*]	[*]The [b]amount of Remains [/b]required for each enchantment level [b]increases significantly[/b][/*][/list]
When Wild Blood launches, there will be an [b]increased amount of tracks and creatures [/b]to allow players to hone their skills. But to keep the new items rare, the additional creatures will drop Silver and loot instead. After a time, these additional creatures will be removed, and those which remain will drop only the new items.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/8926f28f7ce8f4a041f3232edf0facf3c6b492fa.jpeg[/img]

We can’t wait to see players take part in this new economic activity, and start using these new items. You’ll also be able to use them to craft [b]Shapeshifter Weapons, [/b]of course, which will be the subject of our next Dev Talk. See you then!

notes.title: Refer a Friend and Claim the Snow Leopard
notes.content:
[video autoplay="yes" loop="yes" muted="yes" playsinline="yes"]http://assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/video_/media/60f9d68b84e7a_720.mp4[/video]

A new [b]Referral Season[/b] has arrived, and there’s another chance to get the [b]Snow Leopard[/b] when you refer just one friend!

The Snow Leopard is an elegant, hibernal skin for your [b]Swiftclaw[/b] base mount, with snowy gray fur and piercing blue eyes. Once unlocked, it can be used by any of your characters on that particular server (either Albion East or West).

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/eacfbcc119e68dff5c0671e3e27c459f1b9ff8ec.jpeg[/img]

There are also big rewards for your [b]third[/b] and [b]fifth referrals[/b]: a [b]T7 Pile of Tomes worth 100,000 Fame[/b] for your third referral, and a [b]T8 Pile of Tomes worth 200,000 Fame[/b] for your fifth. And for your first ever referral, you’ll get a T8 Pile of Tomes in addition to the Snow Leopard!
[h3]How to Earn Seasonal Referral Rewards[/h3][list]	[*]Send your referral link, which you can find [url=https://albiononline.com/profile/referral/overview][b]here[/b][/url], to a friend. (You must be logged into your account on the website to view this page.)[/*]	[*]Your friend registers an account and starts playing Albion Online (preferably along with you!).[/*]	[*]The first time your friend purchases at least 30 days of Premium, they will trigger a reward for you.[/*]	[*]On top of that, for your very first referral ever, you’ll receive a [b]T8 Recruiter’s Pile of Tomes[/b], worth a massive [b]200,000 Fame[/b].[/*][/list]
This Referral Season lasts until [b]23:59 UTC on October 31[/b], so invite your friends and enjoy these rewards!

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/207ebfea7ec10c15fa5b79aa7f6d7f33adbd8245.png[/img]

notes.title: The Harvest Challenge is Back!
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/06a4dcc5d3f6aacfeed5797945b98b539aa30661.jpeg[/img]

Fall has come to the world of Albion... the shadows are growing longer... and the [b]Harvest Challenge[/b] is back! For the entire month of October, earn points for open-world activities, unlock chests to get spooky loot, and claim your very own [b]Spectral Bat[/b].

[h3][b]Reap What You Sow[/b][/h3]
[b][img]https://assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/my-context/media/5a9e734d7a37c596bd8f341dbc3a91df18612d68.png[/img]
SPECTRAL BAT:[/b] This month's Challenge offers another chance to claim the amazing [b]Spectral Bat[/b]. In addition to its spooky appearance, this winged menace comes with a powerful [b]Flicker[/b] spell that allows you to jump to a target location in the blink of an eye. (Note: like all mounts, the Spectral Bat cannot fly over obstacles or gaps.)

[b][img]https://assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/my-context/media/19075c42b2f6083a97620356e3a682f66f0a4774.png[/img]
AVATAR RING:[/b] Adventurers who rack up enough total Challenge Points will also earn the [b]Harvest Challenge Avatar Ring[/b], featuring a pair of eerie, grinning skeletons. This non-tradable item permanently unlocks this avatar border for one character, or can be traded to the Vanity Merchant for one Vanity Token.

[b][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/2c7ba7c8b9fff4083306b993696b33ec95415878.png[/img][/b]

[b]SEASONAL SPECIALS:[/b] All month long, reach weekly point totals to unlock [b]Harvest Challenge Chests[/b]. Along with valuable rewards like Adventurer's Tomes, Silver, resources, and other loot, you'll also have a chance to unlock six seasonal furniture items: the [b]Scary Pumpkin Lantern, Friendly Pumpkin Lantern, Halloween Lantern, Halloween Cauldron, Halloween Scarecrow,[/b] and [b]Halloween Pyre[/b].

As always, you can earn Challenge Points by [b]gathering, fishing, farming, and killing monsters[/b]. Points count simultaneously toward a daily bonus, a weekly unlockable chest, and the monthly mount and avatar ring reward. So log in, head out into the open world, gather points, and claim these rewards while they last!

[video autoplay="yes" loop="yes" muted="yes" playsinline="yes"]http://assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/df01782c5f310cbc1f408d4a05460c0210d3c4b4.mp4[/video]

notes.title: Dev Talk: Awakened Weapons
notes.content:
Following our recent introduction to the [url=https://albiononline.com/news/dev-talk-islands-farming][b]Island and Farming Rework[/b][/url] coming with the [url=https://albiononline.com/update/wild-blood][b]Wild Blood[/b][/url] update, Game Director Robin Henkys takes a closer look at a massive addition to Albion’s sandbox world: [b]Awakened Weapons[/b].

[previewyoutube=ghbzjoR3sZc;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3]Awakening Weapons[/h3]
Weapons can be awakened:
[list]	[*]At the [b]Artifact Foundry[/b][/*]	[*]If they are [b].4 enchanted[/b][/*]	[*]At the cost of [b]Siphoned Energy[/b], [b]Avalonian Energy[/b], and [b]Silver[/b]	[list]		[*]The exact cost depends on the item’s tier[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
Once awakened, the weapon is [b]attuned[/b] to the player:
[list]	[*][b]Attunement Points[/b] are then earned when you earn PvE Fame[/*]	[*]Weapons of Tier 6 or higher can only earn Attunement Points in [b]full-loot PvP zones[/b][/*][/list]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/955e100f0547786f79ce587fb467a3a213405088.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Traits and Strain[/h3]
When your weapon has enough Attunement Points, Traits can be added at the Artifact Foundry:
[list]	[*]You can choose [b]one of three randomly selected traits[/b] to add[/*]	[*]You can [b]reroll[/b] this, though that will increase Strain on the item (more below)[/*]	[*]Initial values added will be low, but can be increased later at the cost of further [b]Attunement Points[/b]	[list]		[*]This adds a random amount of power to a particular Trait[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Upgrading Traits increases the item’s [b]Legendary Rating[/b]	[list]		[*]As this increases, more Traits can be added[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/17a6ae9d51fc26ddb1b41922e1c02e12e6d906cc.jpeg[/img]

Each action taken on a weapon increases its [b]Strain[/b]. As Strain increases, so does the cost of making further modifications. Therefore, players must consider which Traits to keep and the amount to upgrade them, as the cost in Silver and Attunement Points escalates rapidly.
[h3]Benefits and Legacy[/h3]
Players can customize their .4 weapons this way to add [b]strength and versatility[/b] to their builds, or create a [b]remarkably powerful weapon[/b] if they invest enough time and Silver.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/45ec47b423f1e7bc5b4aa50391c2004e400651d6.jpeg[/img]

But they can also leave a lasting impact on Albion:
[list]	[*]As a weapon’s Legendary Rating increases, its [b]chances of being destroyed on death are reduced[/b][/*]	[*]Therefore, it stands a greater chance of remaining in the game, with [b]a record of its creators and owners[/b][/*]	[*]Players can then choose to add to its history themselves, or trade it - maybe even back to the original owner	[list]		[*]Awakened Weapons [b]cannot be traded on the Marketplace[/b], so this must be done personally[/*]		[*]Traded items (but not looted items) must be [b]re-attuned[/b] to the new owner for their traits to work[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
While these weapons cannot be crafted, Focus Points can be used to [b]reduce the attunement costs[/b] of adding and upgrading traits.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/ef85074e277c0654613de249ae6a642a2bc8136d.jpeg[/img]

Awakened Weapons are a significant addition to Albion’s sandbox world, giving players new possibilities both in combat, and in leaving their mark on the game. Stay tuned for more Dev Talks on the Wild Blood update coming soon!

notes.title: The Next Guild Season Starts Saturday
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/bb26c8b9157957939b014f54677db6e6e428d46b.png[/img]

Albion’s next Guild Season begins this weekend! At 00:00 UTC on September 23, Albion East Season 3 kicks off. And then, at 11:00 UTC, Albion West Season 21 will begin. It looks sure to be an action-packed season, with big rewards on offer like the new [b]Epic[/b] and [b]Legendary Guild Season Winner Direwolf Skins [/b]for multiple season winners! Check [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/185581][b]this forum post[/b][/url] for the full season schedule and list of rewards.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/4372e21ed49306b8cd1dc1be08139ace1cfe685f.jpeg[/img]

[h3]Crystal League Changes[/h3]

As previously announced, this season sees some [b]big changes to the Crystal League[/b]:
[list]	[*]The Crystal League will [b]no longer grant Season Points[/b][/*]	[*]The Lethal Crystal League has been [b]removed entirely[/b], and all 20v20 Crystal League matches are now [b]non-lethal[/b][/*]	[*]At the end of the season, [b]there will no longer be a Crystal League Championship[/b][/*][/list][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/cce8b5e9ab7439b9ba58a0be0f6be676744087ce.jpeg[/img]

As always, you can watch the season kick off this weekend on [url=https://www.twitch.tv/albiononline][b]AlbionTV[/b][/url][b]. [/b]At [b]13:30 UTC[/b] on September 23 we’ll be broadcasting Invasion Day on Albion East. Then at [b]17:30 UTC[/b] we’ll bring coverage from Albion West ahead of the first round of territory resets there. Finally, at [b]00:30 UTC[/b] on September 24, those in the North and South American time zones can tune in for the second round of territory resets on Albion West. All open-world fights are broadcast live with a 15-minute delay.

Check [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/185581][b]this forum post[/b][/url] for a full season schedule, and join us to see the season kickoff!

notes.title: Dev Talk: Islands and Farming Rework
notes.content:
With the [url=https://albiononline.com/update/wild-blood][b]Wild Blood[/b][/url] update arriving [b]October 16[/b], it’s time to take an in-depth look some of its major features. In this Dev Talk, Game Director Robin Henkys and Environment Artist Johannes Geier talk us through the [b]improvements to personal islands and farming [/b]that are on the way.

[previewyoutube=Y98B0IIA4xw;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3]Personal Island Biomes[/h3]
Wild Blood reworks the [b]appearances of all personal islands[/b], with each now belonging to a [b]particular biome[/b].

The goals of this are:
[list]	[*]Give players a [b]visually upgraded[/b] island experience[/*]	[*]Make islands feel secluded while still [b]thematically linked to cities[/b][/*][/list]
[b][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/a3eb5228e80d0082a74cc21297407ab650183f3d.jpeg[/img][/b]

Each island’s visuals will be appropriate to its host city:
[list]	[*][b]Martlock[/b]: Rolling hills, meadows, cliffs, and waterfalls[/*]	[*][b]Lymhurst[/b]: Thick, lush forest with a stream running through[/*]	[*][b]Bridgewatch[/b]: Oasis-like, with warm, shallow waters and palm trees[/*]	[*][b]Fort Sterling[/b]: peaceful, snow-capped mountains[/*]	[*][b]Thetford[/b]: sunken ruins, overgrown trees, and emerald waters[/*]	[*][b]Caerleon[/b]: rough, rocky, bandit-controlled territory[/*][/list]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/fcf8ed860eb09c76542ce71caae757fa46128dde.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Farming Bonuses[/h3]
Along with updated island visuals, new [b]farming bonuses[/b] for crops and animals are being introduced:
[list]	[*]A [b]particular crop[/b] will grow best on each island[/*]	[*]A [b]particular animal[/b] will yield more when butchered on each island[/*]	[*]Each animal will have a [b]favorite food[/b], which makes it grow faster[/*][/list]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/d95ab566ca4b2344aeeffa9d380167e4a743662c.jpeg[/img]

These different bonuses will encourage trade and allow the planning of a sophisticated growing, transportation, and processing schedule.

With these changes on the way, you are now able to [url=https://albiononline.com/news/island-move-2023][b]move an existing island[/b][/url] once until the update launches on [b]October 16[/b]. For details on this and which bonuses apply where, see [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/185792][b]this forum post[/b][/url].

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/4bdc9dbeb28d1461eeef9a24c8736424cda5f105.jpeg[/img]

Furthermore, when Wild Blood releases, players will be able to own [b]multiple personal islands[/b]: up to one for each city, allowing players to build a trans-continental farming empire!

Stay tuned for more Dev Talks on the other Wild Blood features coming very soon.

notes.title: The Final Crystal League Championship: Wrapup
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/372abd39c7f31557102fc3ab97afbafaa577bee2.jpeg[/img]

It is with some sadness that we say farewell to the [b]Crystal League Championship[/b], which took place for the last time at the weekend. But it’s also time to celebrate the achievements of [b]Moral Pro[/b] and [b]Last Season[/b], who took the final titles on East and West respectively!

On Saturday 16 September, the top 8 teams on [b]Albion East[/b] squared off, and after a tough route to the Grand Finale, Moral Pro beat [b]1073 Days[/b] 2-0 to claim the crown. Then, on Sunday 17, Last Season put in a dominant display on [b]Albion West[/b], storming to their ultimate victory with a 2-0 defeat of [b]Mitos[/b], who had made it to the final for the [b]fourth season running[/b].

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/3935aa1b0f38ade52b56d16733eccd4fc00e4335.jpeg[/img]

Congratulations to the top four teams on each server, who took home the following prizes:
[list]	[*][b]First Place[/b]: the extremely rare [b]Saber Tiger Rex [/b]Swiftclaw skin and 10,000 Gold[/*]	[*][b]Second Place[/b]: the [b]Recruiter’s White Tiger[/b] Swiftclaw skinand 5,000 Gold[/*]	[*][b]Third Place[/b]: the [b]Recruiter’s Giant Frog[/b] mount and 5,000 Gold[/*]	[*][b]Fourth Place[/b]: the [b]Occult Cougar Swiftclaw[/b] skin and 5,000 Gold[/*][/list][url=//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/f47f091a420b546f0d30c3946ca0cc34049da84d.jpeg][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/3efb86f711de649024227cb2393a3e6b26fa247a.jpeg[/img][/url]

And with that, the Crystal League Championship comes to an end for the final time. But Albion’s [url=https://albiononline.com/news/season-coming-september-23][b]next Guild Season[/b][/url] is just around the corner, starting September 23, and we hope to see our top 5v5 players continuing to test their mettle in the Crystal Arena and Crystal League. So see you then!

notes.title: Wild Blood is Coming October 16
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/4a91f641db303448452681256a7f5250b0fc9a45.jpeg[/img]

[b]Wild Blood [/b]is drawing close: [b]October 16 [/b]sees the release of Albion’s latest content update, unleashing its primal side. [b]Shapeshifter Weapons [/b]allow players to embody fearsome creatures in combat, while [b]Tracking [/b]lets you hunt them across the open world. New, powerful [b]potions [/b]can be crafted from their remains, and [b]Awakened Items [/b]with unique attributes can be developed through combat. With improvements to [b]player islands[/b] and [b]farming[/b], visually reworked [b]Randomized Dungeons[/b], and more, Wild Blood brings new layers to Albion’s sandbox world.

[h3]Take on New Forms[/h3]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/bbe3e9a632b22414e64b6102594bcb38ef59c128.jpeg[/img]

Wild Blood brings some of Albion’s most primal magic to the fore, which can be harnessed with the all-new [b]Shapeshifter Weapons[/b]. This Staff weapon line lets players [b]metamorphosize into fantastical creatures[/b] mid-combat, expanding the limits of Albion’s ‘you are what you wear’ system. Meanwhile, these beasts can be pursued across the open world in the [b]Tracking [/b]system, and can drop [b]new artifacts and ingredients [/b]to successful hunters, imbued with their magical essence.

[h3]Awaken Your Power[/h3]
The rare, alchemical ingredients dropped by each of these rare beasts can be used to craft [b]brand-new potions[/b] with their own formidable effects, introducing further new combat possibilities, while rare [b]Arcane Extracts [/b]can enchant potions to levels not seen before. And [b]Awakened Items [/b]are coming, which can be [b]imbued with more powerful attributes [/b]through their use in combat, becoming records of their own illustrious past. And while these risk being lost in combat, their [b]unique traits [/b]live on, persisting through Albion’s history as it is written.

[h3]Lands Enriched[/h3]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/06538a075b7a901973d6890b64cc33563d2f2f23.jpeg[/img]

Players can now own [b]multiple Personal Islands[/b], which are each linked to a specific city and have [b]stunning new visuals[/b] to reflect the distinctive atmosphere of each biome. Each of these now has its own [b]farming bonuses [/b]for crops, herbs, and animals, bringing further economic depth to Albion and encouraging trade across the far-flung corners of the Royal Continent. Meanwhile, [b]Randomized Dungeons [/b]have expressive new visuals, reworked layouts, and new enemies. And numerous further improvements are coming too, like the [b]Death Recap[/b], which allows players to review and learn from their defeats in combat, becoming ever more fearsome warriors.

Wild Blood expands the possibilities of life in Albion in new ways, opening up exciting avenues to all types of players. For more details on all this, check the [b]official update page[/b]:

[url=https://albiononline.com/update/wild-blood]LEARN MORE[/url]

notes.title: Guild Season Wrapup: 20 West / 2 East
notes.content:
Another Guild Season is over, and it’s time to announce the winners. So congratulations to [b]Escalation[/b], who won [b]Albion West Season 20[/b], and [b]Winter[/b], who took [b]Albion East Season 2[/b]! Read on for a rundown of each server’s season.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/9ba70d34a083decd561c2d42c59bb5d7bb818a3b.jpeg[/img]

[h3]Albion West: Escalation Claim Second Crown[/h3]

Season 20 started where Season 19 had left off, as the war between the [b]POE[/b] coalition and the [b]XXX [/b]coalition raged on. This would carry on throughout the season, as POE pushed back, and towards the end of the Season the XXX alliance folded, with the [b]FFlow[/b] alliance taking over the coalition to spearhead the fight going into Season 21.

In the north, the [b]Grap3[/b] alliance held their territories against countless attacks throughout the Season, and were able to keep pushing forward as they ended the season with three of their guilds hitting Crystal rank.

Escalation came into the Season declaring victory would be theirs, and they lived up to their word, grinding out open-world objectives and paying out huge amounts of Silver to their Crystal League teams. This led to their second season win, but their greatest achievement was claiming the top spot on the all time Guild PvP Fame charts, ending the season with a total of [b]125.3 billion PvP Fame[/b].

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/871bc1fe316ce43c8983fa3ea05bfe4356fe317f.jpeg[/img]

[h3]Albion East: Winter Go Out On Top[/h3]

As Albion East’s second season got underway, Winter (pictured below - click to expand) announced that they would push for top spot, and they started with a bang, grinding out all the objectives they could in the open world. While that was going on, the battle for second place was going on between [b]GOBLINS[/b] and [b]Order of Ares[/b], and as the season drew to a close this contest really heated up.

With Winter announcing that they'd be folding at the end of the season, many of its members were already joining a new guild: [b]send[/b]. GOBLINS saw an opportunity to secure Winter’s inner-ring territories, which had around 40,000 Season Points in storage, and launched into them, not expecting a strong defense. But Order of Ares were one step ahead, having gotten wind of their plans, and called on their allies to drop their territories for them. Order of Ares held onto sixty territories total on the final day of points payouts, with Winter also massing for one last time as players came back into the guild for one last call to arms, fighting back the attackers and keeping hold of their territories. After the fighting subsided, Winter handed the 40,000 Season Points over to Order of Ares with the territories, allowing them to secure a whopping 110,000 Season Points from territory payouts and launching them into second spot, closing out the season 50,000 points ahead of GOBLINS.

[url=//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/d15d87656c337cb25aa26d7b84587221347b6862.jpeg][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/e056ffdbaf1e98bbb2b4bf1c4b028d0fad64db5e.jpeg[/img][/url]

At the end of the Season, Shy, Winter’s Guildmaster and Shotcaller, had this to say:

"Season 2 on Albion East will be an unforgettable memory for me, and I will always be grateful to all the guild members who followed me. Even though I’m leaving, I hope my fellow Winter members will always be successful."

notes.title: Round Table Reboot: Seeking Quality Feedback!
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/8f07be51271a2f21014474d04d2e6bd18e9ce321.jpeg[/img]

We are excited to announce the launch of a new version of Albion’s [b]Round Table[/b]! This is going to be open to more players than ever before, while still sticking to our original vision of giving our most experienced and well-accomplished players a way to share their knowledge.

[h3]What is the Round Table?[/h3]

At its core, the Round Table is a place for discussion and feedback about the game and its various types of content, where experienced and knowledgeable players come together in a constructive dialogue. The feedback gathered is then forwarded directly to our developers, giving them the opportunity to hear the joys and pains of gameplay first-hand.

With this rework, we’re looking to include experts in as many different playstyles and features as possible.

[b]Applications are now open[/b]! The new iteration starts with the next Guild Season.

We are looking for people who:
[list]	[*][b]Specialize[/b] in specific aspects of the game[/*]	[*]Have [b]long-term experience[/b] in the game[/*]	[*]Are [b]motivated[/b] to help improve the game in every way possible[/*]	[*]Can write [b]feedback[/b] in a polite and constructive way[/*][/list]If this describes you, please head over to [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/186001][b]this Forum post[/b][/url] for more details.

We look forward to seeing you there!

notes.title: Albion’s Next Guild Season Begins Soon
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/aeafaa0a6c7bb4458fdcf185a87105675143391c.jpeg[/img]

The last Guild Season is drawing to a close and the [url=https://albiononline.com/news/final-clc-coming][b]Crystal League Championship[/b][/url] is coming up, but there’s no time for Albion’s guilds to rest on their laurels. Because on [b]September 23[/b], the next season will kick off on both servers!

Great rewards are on offer, including some new prizes available for Albion’s top guilds, and there are also some significant changes to the Crystal League. Read on for more info…

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/4372e21ed49306b8cd1dc1be08139ace1cfe685f.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Season Rewards[/h3]
This season introduces two brand-new rewards: the [b]Epic[/b] and [b]Legendary Guild Season Winner Direwolf Skins. [/b]These eye-catching new skins are rewards for guilds who have won multiple seasons, and can be claimed at the vanity merchant when you have an existing Guild Season Winner Direwolf Skin and a Guild Season Winner unlock item. With these extremely rare skins, guilds who have won either two or three seasons since Guild Season Winner Skins were introduced in Season 19 can proudly display their achievements to the world.

There are, of course, also some fantastic rewards on offer in the Conqueror’s Challenge, like the [b]Crystal Phalanx Beetle[/b], [b]Pyromancer Avatars[/b], and [b]Fame buffs[/b]. For a complete rundown of the prizes on offer, as well as full season schedules, see [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/185581][b]this forum post[/b][/url].

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/4767c99e11fd578721b0f989820ca65a65e70d8d.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Crystal League Changes[/h3]
As previously announced, this season sees some [b]big changes to the Crystal League[/b]:
[list]	[*]The Crystal League will [b]no longer grant Season Points[/b][/*]	[*]The Lethal Crystal League has been [b]removed entirely[/b], and all 20v20 Crystal League matches are now [b]non-lethal[/b][/*]	[*]At the end of the season, [b]there will no longer be a Crystal League Championship[/b][/*][/list]
[b][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/cce8b5e9ab7439b9ba58a0be0f6be676744087ce.jpeg[/img][/b]
[h3]Times and Broadcasts[/h3]
The season kicks off on September 23 at [b]00:00 UTC on Albion East [/b](that is: 08:00 on September 23 in Singapore; 20:00 on September 22 in Washington, D.C.), and [b]11:00 UTC on Albion West[/b]. And as always, you can watch it all kick off on [url=https://www.twitch.tv/albiononline][b]AlbionTV[/b][/url][b].[/b]

At [b]13:30 UTC[/b] on September 23 we’ll be broadcasting Invasion Day on Albion East. Then at [b]17:30 UTC[/b] we’ll bring coverage from Albion West ahead of the first round of territory resets there. Finally, at [b]00:30 UTC[/b] on September 24, those in the North and South American time zones can tune in for the second round of territory resets on Albion West. All open-world fights are broadcast live with a 15-minute delay.

Check [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/185581][b]this forum post[/b][/url] for a full season schedule, and join us to see the season kickoff!

notes.title: The Final Crystal League Championship is Coming
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/d8db78c4d4adc377d5c945e7ac25f85a7d32f0e8.jpeg[/img]

The Crystal League Championship is coming [b]September 16-17[/b], and as always, there are big prizes up for grabs! But this will be a bittersweet event, as unfortunately this will be Albion’s [b]last CLC[/b]. Read on for more info…
[h3]Crystal League Changes[/h3]
We’ve seen some fantastic moments in these tournaments, and we truly appreciate the passion and joy with which our players took part. But it’s time to move forward, and following this tournament the [b]Lethal Crystal League will be removed from the game altogether[/b]. Furthermore, the Crystal League will [b]no longer grant Season Points[/b] from the beginning of next season, in order to place a greater emphasis on other guild activities.

While this is of course a big change for our Crystal League players, we trust that our community can stage their own exciting tournaments and perhaps other competitive formats, and we’ll support [b]Custom Matches[/b] with a new [b]Observer Mode[/b] to encourage this.

In the meantime, let’s look ahead to what’s sure to be another exciting Crystal League Championship, and send it off with a bang!

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/939b8d635e1be87c9afb1f232a7a0219fa555025.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Times and Prizes[/h3]
The tournament will take place at the following times on each server:
[list]	[*][b]Albion East[/b]: September 16 at 10:00 UTC[/*]	[*][b]Albion West[/b]: September 17 at 17:00 UTC[/*][/list]
The following prizes are available to each member of the top four teams in each tournament:
[list]	[*]First place: [b]Saber Tiger Rex[/b] Swiftclaw skin and [b]10,000 Gold[/b][/*]	[*]Second place: [b]Recruiter’s White Tiger[/b] Swiftclaw skin and [b]5,000 Gold[/b][/*]	[*]Third place: [b]Recruiter’s Giant Frog[/b] mount and [b]5,000 Gold[/b][/*]	[*]Fourth place: [b]Occult Cougar[/b] Swiftclaw skin and [b]5,000 Gold[/b][/*][/list]
[b][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/7783620a6e970fcf4a248e8c3fd28efa59fb17b3.png[/img][/b]
[h3]Changes[/h3]
This edition of the CLC sees a few changes from the previous one:
[list]	[*]A team must have [b]five consistent players [/b]to earn points; so, any changed line-ups during the season count as a separate team with its own points. (Note: during the tournament, substitutes are still permitted).[/*]	[*]This time, the [b]top six Non-Lethal[/b] and [b]top two Lethal Crystal League[/b] teams on each server will qualify.[/*]	[*]To make the tournament progress faster, teams now have [b]one minute[/b] to accept their match invitation, or they will receive a strike[/*][/list]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/5368aafa7c820964d76b4140bc50d9b6f6042c4b.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Watch Live on AlbionTV[/h3]
And of course, you can tune in to see the final edition of the CLC on [url=https://www.twitch.tv/albiononline][b]AlbionTV[/b][/url] across the weekend! Hosts Shozen, [b]Lewpac[/b], and [b]Tazzik[/b] will be bringing you live coverage of the tournaments on Albion East and West, from [b]10:00 UTC on September 16[/b] and from [b]17:00 UTC on September 17[/b]. And as always, the champions will be crowned and receive their prizes at a ceremony after the event.

We hope you join us for what’s sure to be an emotional but unforgettable event. Keep an eye on the [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/185266][b]forum[/b][/url] for updates, and we’ll see you for the tournament!

notes.title: Guide: Crafting
notes.content:
[b]Crafting[/b] is one of the foremost components of Albion's player-driven economy. While excelling as a crafter requires hard work and planning, when done properly it can be one of the most rewarding activities in the game. This guide will start you on your way to being a skilled crafter with a few essential tips.

Once you have completed the first part of the tutorial, you will unlock Novice Adventurer in the Destiny Board, which will in turn unlock the [b]Trainee Craftsman Mastery[/b]. This node allows you to craft Novice items at four different types of crafting station: [b]Mage's Tower[/b], [b]Warrior's Forge[/b], [b]Hunter's Lodge[/b] and [b]Toolmaker[/b].

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/3782c2de696fdaaf0b4e0d76eb5eaf46d92379e3.jpeg[/img]

From this point on you will always have the choice between being self-sufficient by gathering and refining the materials needed or buying already-refined materials from the marketplace.

Here’s an overview of all the different [b]crafting stations[/b] and the respective items you can craft there:

[table]			[tr]			[td]			
[b]Crafting Station[/b]
			[/td]			[td]			
[b]Weapons[/b]
			[/td]			[td]			
[b]Armors[/b]
			[/td]		[/tr]		[tr]			[td]			
Warrior’s Forge
			[/td]			[td]			
Swords, Axes, Maces, Hammers, Crossbows, War Gloves, Shields
			[/td]			[td]			
Plate Helmets, Armors & Boots
			[/td]		[/tr]		[tr]			[td]			
Hunter’s Lodge
			[/td]			[td]			
Bows, Spears, Nature Staffs, Daggers, Quarterstaffs, Torches
			[/td]			[td]			
Leather Hoods, Jackets & Shoes
			[/td]		[/tr]		[tr]			[td]			
Mage’s Tower
			[/td]			[td]			
Fire, Holy, Arcane, Frost, and Cursed Staffs, Tomes
			[/td]			[td]			
Cloth Cowls, Robes & Sandals
			[/td]		[/tr]		[tr]			[td]			
Toolmaker
			[/td]			[td]			
Gathering tools, Demolition Hammers
			[/td]			[td]			
Gathering gear, Capes & Bags
			[/td]		[/tr]	[/table]
[h3]Studying Items[/h3]

If you want to make faster progress in your crafting mastery you have the option to [b]study [/b]an item. This gives you a minimum of [b]275% of the crafting Fame[/b] of the item you are studying. When you add this to the 100% Fame received for crafting the item, the result is a huge bonus that will allow you to quickly unlock Journeyman or Adept crafting levels. The downside is that items are destroyed when studied, but the benefits far outweigh the disadvantages for progression purposes. It is important to understand that each item you wish to study [b]has to be studied at the correct crafting station[/b] - so a Broadsword is studied at a Warrior’s Forge, a Mercenary Jacket at a Hunter's Lodge, and so on.

[url=//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/f23baea708bd76a528734b3b921abd8fdb8dbe53.jpeg][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/170b28c6cc52ce4a4387636971c0bc4020dda4c4.jpeg[/img][/url]

Once you have unlocked T4 crafting for a given item [b]you will no longer be able to study the tiers of equipment below it[/b], so you can’t just craft huge amounts of Novice or Journeyman gear and study all the way to Expert. Instead, you should work out how many items you need to craft and study to get to the next tier with a minimum of resources used. [b]Planning ahead when crafting is vital![/b]

[h3]Resource Return[/h3]

When crafting at a player station in a [b]city[/b], the [b]Outlands[/b] or a [b]Hideout,[/b] you will gain a bonus on resource return. As the name suggests, this will [b]return a percentage of the resources to you when crafting[/b]. But be aware that, since crafting stations in the cities are player-run, they usually apply a crafting fee. Make sure to check the crafting tax before beginning to craft.

[h3]Local Production Bonuses[/h3]

Local production bonuses are added to the normal resource return and reward you for crafting or refining items [b]in a specific location[/b]. Each biome has a bonus for one refined resource along with several weapons and armor pieces. For example: the Forest biome provides bonuses to cloth refining, and Bow, Sword, Arcane Staff, Leather Hood and Shoe crafting. This means that there is an increased return when crafting these items in the city of Lymhurst or in a Hideout in a forest biome. [b]Cities always provide the best[/b] resource returns for [b]refining,[/b] while [b]Hideouts[/b] [b]provide better[/b] resource returns for [b]gear[/b]. The return also scales with zone quality and Hideout level.

Local production bonuses are listed in the top-right of the overview map. The numbers displayed show how many [b]more items can be generated if returned resources are reinvested[/b].

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/2f73c84a476baba8e21f5555ebebb44139693d97.jpeg[/img]

[h3]Daily Production Bonus[/h3]

Crafters who want to further maximize their efficiency can take advantage of the [b]Activities window[/b], where you can see the [b]daily production bonus[/b]. This changes each day with maintenance and offers a 10% or 20% production bonus on up to two different item groups.

[h3]Focus[/h3]

[b]Focus[/b] is an invaluable tool for any artisan. Turning Focus on allows you to increase the return rate of materials used in crafting. Focus recharges at 10,000 points a day for characters with Premium - refilling gradually throughout the day rather than in a single deposit.

To craft using Focus, check the [b]Focus box[/b] at the bottom of the crafting window (see image below). The number displayed will show how much Focus you need for an increased return of resources. Some items take a huge amount of Focus to get the full return bonus, so check before you craft.

When using Focus make sure to prioritize items that use expensive resources, and always consider these new bonuses before crafting. Any increased bonus means increased profit for you, as getting more materials back allows you to make more items with your valued resources.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/79a2a819953ed85223448f131122e36224298505.jpeg[/img]

[h3]Item Quality[/h3]

Before clicking "Craft", ensure you have enough Focus, else a lower resource return will be applied. Make sure to select not only the correct item, but also the desired [b]enchantment level[/b]. Once you're ready, click the Focus box, and click Craft. Bring your force of will upon the item, and hope for a masterpiece!

When you craft a Journeyman’s item, it will have a base item power of 500. This is [b]modified by quality[/b], which can be very important as it often dictates the price the finished item can be sold for, or what bonuses they add when used in combat. Let us look at quality bonuses in the image below.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/170c4f883558bc6582a01ee5c3c3eeb1038e45d6.jpeg[/img]

To further boost your chances of crafting higher quality items, or to simply speed up the crafting process, you can eat salads before you begin. These offer a two-minute buff during which the chances of crafting higher quality items is increased, along with crafting speed.

[h3]Crafting Mastery & Specialization[/h3]

When leveling up a crafting profession you will mostly pay attention to the [b]Crafting Mastery[/b] of your item category. This is the main node that determines the tier of items you can craft in a specific item category. In addition to unlocking the ability to craft higher tiers, you will also gain a small bonus towards Focus cost efficiency, and a higher chance of crafting better quality items.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/88c887ae0c06b6a49f44495161337c42bea701db.jpeg[/img]

The Mastery node splits up into a node for each separate item that can be crafted. Each of the 7 different Fire Staffs above has their own [b]Specialization[/b]. Leveling these will grant a [b]huge bonus[/b] to Focus cost efficiency and item quality chances for that [b]specific item,[/b] while also granting a [b]small bonus[/b] to [b]all other Fire Staffs[/b].

When crafting an item of Adept level or higher, you will always gain Fame towards the [b]Mastery and Specialization[/b] node.

You can see how important [b]Study, Mastery, and Specialization[/b] are to crafting, and their effects on item levels. Now we need to look at how using [b]enchanted materials[/b] from Adept level upwards affects an item's stats as well.

[h3]Enchanted gear[/h3]

To craft with enchanted materials, first enter the crafting menu as if you were crafting an item with normal materials. In the crafting box you will see four diamonds, which signify the enchantment levels of materials you wish to craft with. [b]The green diamond allows you to craft .1 (Uncommon), the blue diamond allows you to craft .2 (Rare),  the purple diamond allows you to craft .3 (Exceptional) and the gold diamond allows you to craft .4 (Pristine)[/b]. Simply select the level of enchantment by clicking the corresponding diamond, and if you have the correct materials you will be able to craft the item. Bear in mind that if the item requires multiple material types, all of the materials must be enchanted and all must be of the same level!

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/e26bfdfb7286488dbec771a86f07350249bd0020.jpeg[/img]

Enchanted items also have a [b]tier bonus[/b] as detailed in the picture below. This is a huge factor when it comes to selling items, as enchanted items of higher quality are sought after and command high prices!

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/246899bf6d72184e22fb291c991b5eeaaa905a90.jpeg[/img]

It is also important to note that, when crafting high-level items, you will need to have a [b]plan to source the materials[/b]. This can be done either by raising your gathering and refining levels so you can produce the materials yourself, or purchasing the required materials. If purchasing the materials yourself, it is a good idea to use buy orders on the Marketplace to get the materials as cheaply as possible and maximize your profit or study potential.

If you’ve crafted an item with high quality but low enchantment, you can also enchant them later on at the [b]Artifact Foundry[/b].

[h3]Artifacts[/h3]

Speaking of Artifacts, it is important to know the different types of Artifact - both in terms of item power level and where we can source the materials to make these pieces of sought-after equipment.

There are four levels of Artifact materials:
[list]	[*]Level 1: [b]Runes[/b] (Artifact) or [b]Royal Sigils[/b][/*]	[*]Level 2: [b]Souls[/b] (Artifact)[/*]	[*]Level 3: [b]Relics[/b] (Artifact) or [b]Feys[/b][/*]	[*]Level 4: [b]Avalonian Shards[/b][/*][/list]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/1af1685a3493f26ae968bd4e4c847e27cdfd10a2.jpeg[/img]

You can craft all Artifacts, except for Royal Sigils (exclusive to Arenas and Expeditions) and Fey artifacts (Exclusive to the Mists), at the [b]Artifact Foundry[/b], found in every city. Runes, Souls and Relics can be found in various places such as the open world, dungeons or Hellgates - the higher the zone tier, the higher the level of materials you'll find. You may even get an Artifact or Artifact piece straight away as a random drop!

[h3]What to do now?[/h3]
You may wonder if there’s even demand for all the gear you’re crafting, and where you should sell it.

First of all, there is high demand for all sorts of gear due to so many players engaging in [b]full-loot PvP fights[/b] all over Albion, meaning when a player dies in PvP combat, each item he was wearing or carrying has [b]a chance to break[/b]. And while you can sell your gear in the thriving Marketplaces of each city or directly to other players, there is also the option to bring your goods to the Black Market in Caerleon. There, a sinister trader buys [b]large quantities[/b] of equipment which are distributed to every individual mob or chest in the game.

notes.title: Dev Talk: Awakened and Legendary Items
notes.content:
Following our recent introductions to [url=https://albiononline.com/news/devtalk-shapeshifter][b]Shapeshifter[/b][/url] weapons and [url=https://albiononline.com/news/devtalk-tracking][b]Tracking[/b][/url], our newest Dev Talk with Game Director Robin Henkys explores another exciting feature on its way to Albion: [b]Awakened [/b]and [b]Legendary Items[/b].

[previewyoutube=uvuB5unjaeE?rel=0;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3]Goals[/h3][list]	[*]Add one-of-a-kind items with their [b]own story [/b]to the game[/*]	[*]These won’t be pre-designed, but [b]created by players[/b][/*]	[*]These will be [b]very rare[/b], with each feeling like a significant piece of the world of Albion[/*][/list][h3]How does it work?[/h3]
Creating Legendary Items will be a [b]two-stage process[/b]:
[list]	[*]First, an item will need to be [b]awakened[/b][/*]	[*]Then, eventually, it can be made [b]legendary[/b][/*][/list]
[b][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/b0a979750a48495260c4e8f346f1a129392d4a42.jpeg[/img][/b]

[b]Awakened Items[/b]
[list]	[*][b]Awakened Weapons [/b]will arrive with Albion’s next content update[/*]	[*]A weapon must have [b]Pristine Enchantment [/b]before it can be awakened[/*]	[*]Awakened weapons can earn [b]attunement points [/b]from PvE combat	[list]		[*]These can be used to roll for [b]additional or improved traits [/b]on the weapon[/*]		[*]Such modifications add [b]strain [/b]to the weapon, increasing the cost of further changes[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Players can thus create weapons with [b]unique traits[/b], with the increasing cost of modifications encouraging a [b]variety of trait combinations[/b][/*][/list]
[b][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/6a76872fea4433b669680712b07114b597cedaa4.jpeg[/img][/b]

[b]Legendary Rating[/b]
[list]	[*]As weapons gain more powerful traits, their [b]legendary rating [/b]increases[/*]	[*]This also [b]increases the likelihood [/b]of it being lost or destroyed on death[/*]	[*]Lost items can return to the game as loot, with their [b]creator’s name attached[/b][/*]	[*]They can then be [b]further attuned[/b], with further players adding their name to its history[/*][/list]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/9864134bdfaa47a3f715b45f5116b6076cb4af47.jpeg[/img]

A later content update will introduce the ability to upgrade items to legendary status. These will require extremely rare resources, but will be [b]uniquely powerful and renowned across Albion[/b].

Thanks for reading, and stay tuned for more on our upcoming update and further plans!
