notes.title: Season 13 Starts Saturday
notes.content:
Saturday marks the beginning of Albion's [b]thirteenth Guild Season[/b], with numerous updates to open-world gameplay and an incredible new battle mount, the [b]Phalanx Beetle[/b], as a season reward. The recently released [url=https://albiononline.com/news/cta-patch-7-is-here][b]Season 13 Patch[/b][/url] introduced new and updated open-world content including two new high-level enemies, increases to Fame and Season Points for killing open-world mobs, greatly increased resource and enchanted resource spawn rates, updated castle layouts and loot, and an adjusted Crystal League schedule.

And to celebrate the upcoming season, we've created a brand-new trailer:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RIzB8ap_sjY
[h3]New Season Rewards[/h3]
Guilds that reach a high enough rank can claim fantastic rewards including an [b]avatar,[/b] [b]avatar ring,[/b] and the mighty [b]Phalanx Beetle [/b]mount. This mount will be awarded to guilds who reach [b]Silver Rank or higher[/b] during Season 13, with increasingly higher stats and epic appearance with each successive tier.

As always, the winning guild will receive a statue among the past Guild Season winners in Conquerors' Hall, and qualifying guilds will also receive a Fame Bonus and furniture items. For full Season Rewards details, see [url=https://albiononline.com/news/season-13-rewards][b]this article[/b][/url].

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/aeafaa0a6c7bb4458fdcf185a87105675143391c.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Season 13 Changes[/h3]
Season 13 doubles Fame earned for killing Siphoning Mages and open-world mobs, and introduces two new open-world enemies: the Treasure Drone and the Crystal Spider. Gathering has been boosted with increased resource enchantment rates, and the loot of Castle Outpost chests has been doubled. Further adjustments have been made to Disarray, Castle layouts, and the 20v20 Crystal League to keep seasonal guild warfare competitive and fair.

Season 13 brings big changes, including:
[list]	[*][b]Resource and Transmutation [/b]changes[/*]	[*][b]20v20 Crystal League schedule[/b] adjustments[/*]	[*][b]Disarray curve [/b]adjustments[/*]	[*][b]Shield bubbles from instances[/b] shortened[/*]	[*][b]Combat Balance[/b] adjustments[/*]	[*]...and much more[/*][/list]

notes.title: Call to Arms Patch 7 is Here
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/1957905f0fe184f22f277148f99ca4f81e0d61ea.jpeg[/img]

Call to Arms Patch 7, AKA the [b]Season 13 Patch[/b], is now live! This patch brings big changes and improvements to [b]competitive open-world gameplay[/b] in Albion. As Albion's next major content update will be focused on improving the overall [b]open-world experience[/b] (more about that soon!), we've decided to bring some of those changes to the game already, in anticipation of the start of [b]Guild Season 13[/b] this Saturday.
[h3]New Mobs: Crystal Spider and Treasure Drone[/h3]
The [b]Crystal Spider[/b] is a new rare boss that randomly spawns throughout the Outlands, intended for groups of 3-5 players. In addition to Fame, killing a Crystal Spider grants up to 30 [b]Season Points[/b]. [b]Treasure Drones[/b] are rare mobs that transport Avalonian Chests through the open world, and are defeatable by solo adventurers. They have similar rarity levels to dungeon chests, with higher-tier drones dropping increasingly valuable [b]Avalonian loot[/b].

Other mob changes include world boss spawn times being doubled to two hours, as well as [b]double Season Points[/b] for killing world bosses and [b]double Fame[/b] for all open-world faction mobs and Siphoning Mages.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/599e830da9e5ef1cb10fc01160d557357baa640a.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Resource and Transmutation Changes[/h3]
The spawn rate of enchanted resources has increased, with rare resources [b]doubled[/b] and exceptional resources [b]quadrupled[/b]. [b]Resource transmutation prices[/b] have overall been increased, as has the respawn rate of all [b]T5+ resources[/b] in the open world. At the same time, transmutation prices for Runes, Souls, and Relics have been [b]significantly reduced[/b] to make high-level Artifacts cheaper to craft and more accessible.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/a5123f87baa91d724097dda131bf1a00a8c0458b.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Additional Changes[/h3][list]	[*][b]Castle layouts[/b] adjusted; [b]Castle Outpost chest loot[/b] doubled[/*]	[*][b]20v20 Crystal League schedule[/b] adjusted[/*]	[*][b]Disarray (Zerg debuff) curve adjusted[/b] to be much steeper[/*]	[*][b]Shield bubbles from instances[/b] shortened[/*]	[*]Corpses can no longer be looted while Hellgate [b]PvP [/b]is active[/*]	[*]Four new [b]Avatar Rings[/b] added to Vanity Merchant[/*]	[*][b]Combat Balance[/b] adjustments[/*]	[*]...and much more[/*][/list]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/28d13609f838b81e67931b362a2d067fa8106b2b.jpeg[/img]

You can check out the [url=https://albiononline.com/changelog/CALL%20TO%20ARMS%20PATCH%207][b]official patchnotes[/b][/url] for the complete list of changes, improvements, and fixes.
[h3]Season 13 Starts Saturday[/h3]
Albion's next Guild Season is almost upon us, with incredible rewards for ranking guilds including the [url=https://albiononline.com/news/season-13-rewards][b]Phalanx Beetle[/b][/url]. You can check out the full Season 13 schedule right [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/150011][b]here[/b][/url]. We'll see you soon ingame!

notes.title: Albion Online’s Popularity Hits Record Level
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/bc7a03f3939b9ae1286363d54533c363cee6a5ad.jpeg[/img]

2021 has seen Albion's population grow bigger than ever before, with Daily Average User counts increasing even beyond the previous records set in 2020. In February, the game reached a new peak of [b]135,000 daily active players[/b], which was immediately surpassed with the launch of the [url=https://albiononline.com/en/update/call-to-arms][b]Call to Arms[/b][/url] update in March. With its complete rework of [b]Faction Warfare[/b], revamped [b]Hellgates[/b], [b]Loadouts[/b], and much more, Call to Arms pushed Albion's daily average population to over [b]140,000[/b] and also saw some of the game's highest-ever numbers on Twitch and Youtube.

Peak player numbers on [b]Steam [/b]also increased by over 200% since January of last year, reaching a peak of nearly [b]13,000 simultaneous Steam players[/b] in addition to the majority playing via native platforms.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/dcd0097aef7fb34ddbd4160f0ae1ee2d5054aea6.png[/img]
[h3]Albion's Mobile Launch: Shattering Previous Records[/h3]
On June 9, 2021, Albion's mobile version went live worldwide on the Apple App Store and Google Play Store. The launch was the result of years of development and optimizations, and finally fulfilled the goal – set out in the game's very earliest stages of development – of offering a truly cross-platform sandbox MMORPG experience. After the game went live on the App and Play Stores, new and returning players flooded into the game, setting a staggering new record: [b]270,000 daily active players[/b], nearly twice the previous peak.

The mobile launch brought an exclusive reward, consisting of the brand-new [b]Chimera Riding Horse Skin[/b] and 100,000 Fame, given to all players who log into the game on both desktop and mobile. Along with this reward, the celebration of Albion's status as a truly cross-platform experience was rounded out with the launch of a new [b]live-action trailer[/b]. (You can read more about the launch rewards and watch the trailer [url=https://albiononline.com/news/mobile-version-out-now][b]here[/b][/url].)

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/c8dbf5ad8455bf2bbe51b739c940791173322616.jpeg[/img]
[h3]What's Next?[/h3]
As mentioned in our last update, we're already hard at work on our next major content update later this year, which will focus on improving and deepening Albion's [b]open world[/b]. You can look forward to a Roadmap Update from our Game Director soon, which will cover our plans for the coming months and give a preview of some of the specific features currently in the works.

To veteran and returning players, thanks for being part of the world of Albion and making it what it is today. And to new players, we would like to extend a warm welcome to the Albion community!

For now, we're incredibly proud of what we've accomplished along with our community, our supporters, and all our past and present team members who made this incredible milestone – for both the game, and the genre as a whole – possible. A heartfelt [b]thank you[/b] from the entire Albion Online team!

notes.title: Albion Online Launches for Mobile on June 9!
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/895090c83c58b54e0724d654b9eccc8430cb64c7.jpeg[/img]

It's official: Albion Online launches worldwide on the Apple App Store and Google Play Store on [b]June 9, 2021[/b]! This launch is the culmination of years of upgrades and improvements, and fulfills Albion Online's cross-play promise of delivering [b]the full PC experience on mobile devices[/b]. Be sure to [url=https://albiononline.com/pre-register][b]pre-register now[/b][/url] to be notified when the mobile version is live!

To celebrate the launch, all players will be eligible for a [b]cross-platform reward[/b] once the mobile version is officially released. This reward consists of the new [b]Chimera Riding Horse Skin[/b] and Tomes of Insight worth [b]100,000 Fame[/b], and will be awarded to all players who log into both the desktop and mobile version of the game after the launch on June 9.

Game Director [b]Robin Henkys[/b] gives highlights of the mobile version and details of the launch in his latest Dev Talk:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MfzoDXd5v5Y
Prefer a written summary? Read on...
[h3]A True Cross-Platform Experience[/h3]
Albion Online was conceived nine years ago with a clear goal: to create a deep and meaningful player-driven sandbox MMORPG that was as accessible as possible. The ultimate accessibility goal was for players to be able to get [b]the full PC experience wherever they were, and on whatever platform they chose[/b], including [b]iOS and Android devices[/b].

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/2f7c23d8e55fd9f1efe5c7fcb4774d1c4c093b5d.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Developing the Mobile Version[/h3]
Creating Albion's mobile version presented several unique challenges:
[list]	[*][b]Making complex features accessible[/b] with the limited space available on mobile screens[/*]	[*][b]Adapting controls[/b] from mouse to touch controls to ensure mobile players can compete with PC players[/*]	[*][b]Optimizing memory usage[/b] and performance to run in the significantly more limited hardware environment of mobile devices[/*][/list]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/49d4f0f1869a1b368e023f10ad7010002fee1386.jpeg[/img]

notes.title: Patch 4 Brings Big Hellgate and Balance Changes
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/dffe36cf0c3bcb3687bfed2057eb626260504446.jpeg[/img]

Call to Arms Patch 4, AKA the [b]Call to Arms Balance Patch[/b], is here! First and foremost, this patch brings big changes and improvements to all types of [b]Hellgates[/b], including [b]massively increased rewards[/b], improved [b]matchmaking[/b], an automatic [b]cooldown reset[/b] when invaded, and streamlined [b]knockdown mechanics[/b].

Additionally, Patch 4 brings a huge array of [b]Combat Balance Changes[/b] across numerous weapon and armor lines, along with updates and improvements to [b]Faction Warfare[/b], the [b]20v20 Crystal League[/b], the [b]Black Zone Fame Buff[/b], and more.
[h3]Hellgates: Better Rewards and Matchmaking[/h3]
We've made numerous improvements to the overall experience in all sizes and types of Hellgates based on testing and community feedback. Here are some of the biggest changes:
[list]	[*][b]Significantly increased rewards[/b] across all Hellgate modes[/*]	[*]Chests now [b]always spawn[/b] once a Hellgate is complete, whether or not PvP occurred[/*]	[*][b]Cooldowns and Health [/b]now reset after an invasion[/*]	[*]Removed matchmaking delay in [b]chained Hellgates[/b][/*][/list][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/2e3338400750ef56e57d10ffb880fa1a5418a75d.jpeg[/img][h3]Combat Balance Changes[/h3]
Michael Schwahn, Albion's Combat Designer, sums up the balance changes in this patch:

[i]"This patch aims to bring a wider variety of healing staffs into the meta while reducing the dominance of certain items in specific content, like Dagger Pairs in 2v2 Hellgates and Quarterstaffs in Corrupted Dungeons. Sustain damage provided by the axe line is also reduced, to bring them more in line with other melee weapons. This patch also offers reworks of abilities that have been out of the spotlight recently."[/i]

Here's a partial list of what's new:
[list]	[*][b]Axes:[/b] Updated numerous skills to increase importance of positioning and timing[/*]	[*][b]Cursed Staffs:[/b] Buffed various skills to improve performance in PvP[/*]	[*][b]Nature Staffs:[/b] Added a burst-heal W-slot ability[/*]	[*][b]Armors:[/b] Updated Life Steal Aura and Self-Ignition[/*][/list][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/c666be2ddf88b11e28f238ab6cdce2907b87aad1.jpeg[/img][h3]Other Changes[/h3][list]	[*][b]Improved load times[/b] between zones on all platforms[/*]	[*][b]Faction Warfare: Respawns[/b] now happen in batches to help rally forces; [b]Bandit Assault[/b] is more frequent and unpredictable[/*]	[*][b]20v20 Crystal League: [/b]Increased [b]artifact rewards[/b] in final chests[/*]	[*][b]Black Zone Fame Buff [/b]persists when [b]moving between zones[/b][/*]	[*][b]Mobile Version:[/b] Further optimizations and UI improvements[/*]	[*]… and much more[/*][/list]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/947cb7027ae6bc9a3ae0cab562dbb17383ad40a5.jpeg[/img]

Finally, for this patch, we're also trying something new: offering [b]detailed explanations of combat balance changes[/b] under each weapon and armor type, to show the reasons and goals behind them. As always, you can check out the full list of changes, including these detailed balance change descriptions, in the [url=https://albiononline.com/en/changelog/CALL%20TO%20ARMS%20PATCH%204][b]official patchnotes[/b][/url].

notes.title: Population Update: Spring 2021
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/4f4cb9437947e63fdc4eab6d5f585829a406bf14.jpeg[/img]

2020 saw Albion's population grow bigger than ever before, with Daily Average User counts increasing consistently throughout the year. Starting with the Queen Update in January and growing further during the worldwide lockdowns that followed, the population hit a new milestone nearly every month. The massive [url=https://albiononline.com/en/update/rise-of-avalon][b]Rise of Avalon[/b] [b]update[/b][/url] followed in August, bringing a host of new features and two new languages to the game, and by September the Daily Average User count surpassed[b] [url=https://albiononline.com/en/news/population-update-september-2020]125,000 players[/url][/b].

This trend continued into 2021, reaching a new peak of [b]135,000 players[/b] in February. Then, on March 17, the [url=https://albiononline.com/en/update/call-to-arms][b]Call to Arms[/b][/url] update went live, bringing a ground-up rework of [b]Faction Warfare[/b], completely revamped [b]Hellgates[/b], [b]Loadouts[/b], and much more. The combined influx of new and returning players with this launch pushed Albion's daily average population to over [b]140,000[/b], and also saw some of the game's highest-ever numbers on Twitch and Youtube.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/9b8153d392cfdcd06d0850b6a780411dbd673461.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Looking Forward to 2021[/h3]
So what's next for the world of Albion? First off, we're hard at work on the [b]mobile version[/b], and are putting the final pieces in place for the [b]official Apple and Google store launches[/b]. We'll have some exciting updates soon on the mobile version, so stay tuned. And of course, we're already looking forward to the next big steps for the game, including our next major content update later this year, which will focus on improving and deepening Albion's open world.

To veteran and returning players, thanks for being part of the world of Albion and making it what it is today. And to new players, we would like to extend a warm welcome to the Albion community – be sure to visit our [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/][b]forum[/b][/url] with any questions, and keep an eye out for [b]new player video guides[/b] coming soon!

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/1f557a77d35faaab76cfc6b838c9a7f4107239dd.png[/img]

Decorations have appeared in Albion's cities, and colorful eggs have sprouted throughout the open world. Break these mysterious giant eggs open to gather [b]Surprise Eggs[/b], which can be spent at the Vanity Merchant or thrown to hatch a surprise of their own!

notes.title: Call to Arms Patch 1 is Here
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/bad5c3bb49ca5f0cfb38be8ba38b17eb0587b1c5.jpeg[/img]

The first patch of the [b]Call to Arms[/b] update is now live! This patch brings optimizations and adjustments to the update's two primary features, [b]Faction Warfare[/b] and [b]Hellgates[/b], along with other changes and fixes and a brand-new [b]Premiere Mount Skin[/b]. Read on for all the details...
[h3]New Riding Horse Skin: Hell Mare[/h3]
The new [b]Hell Mare[/b] Mount Skin turns any Riding Horse base mount into a dark and demonic infernal beast. This skin is available in the ingame store, and once purchased can be applied to all characters on your account forever. Pick one up today and blaze a fiery path across Albion!
[h3]Guild Season Winner Statue Added[/h3]
Congratulations to [b]Black 0rder[/b] on their second consecutive season win! You can check out their statue at the entrance to Conquerors' Hall.
[h3][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/89af6ee16de84f069c0ca7d808eece6291dc161e.jpeg[/img][/h3][h3]Faction Warfare Changes[/h3]
The launch of Call to Arms saw a massive influx of players participating in [b]Faction Warfare[/b], which exceeded even our high-end expectations. As the system is based on a set number of points for players to fight over, we've [b]significantly increased the overall points available[/b] to give individual players a better return on their efforts. We've also greatly reduced the [b]point requirements[/b] for daily Faction Campaign bonuses, and we'll be reducing the overall campaign milestone requirements as well starting next month.

We're thrilled at the overwhelming response to the Faction Warfare rework, and we'll continue to keep an eye on this feature to make sure it remains fun, challenging, and rewarding for all players.
[h3]Crystal League Updates: Artifacts and No-Show Points[/h3]
Level 2 and higher 20v20 Crystal League rewards now always include [b]artifacts[/b], with a rare chance of being extremely valuable [b]Avalonian artifacts[/b]. Additionally, if no matchup is found, both 5v5 and 20v20 teams will now receive [b]80% of the available Season Points[/b] (previously 60%).

For a complete list of changes, check out the [url=https://albiononline.com/en/changelog/CALL%20TO%20ARMS%20PATCH%201][b]official patchnotes[/b][/url].

notes.title: Design Showcase: Hellgates
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/bfc70070c1c0d8a841d8d0a2549524921765fbcb.jpeg[/img]

The [b]Call to Arms [/b]update arrives March 17, bringing a complete [b]Hellgate rework[/b] along with other features. We discussed the changes coming to Hellgates with Environment Art Director [b]Stefan Warias[/b] and Level Designer [b]Dominik Müller[/b].

[b]The new Hellgate entrances are much more detailed than the old ones. What sort of information do they convey?[/b]

[b]SW:[/b] Visually the goal for the entrances was to reflect the theme and atmosphere of the levels they lead to. After some design iterations we came up with physical elements like sharp rocks, which are the main elements in the hellish environment. And they behave as if possessed by a demon, with animations and FX that bring them to life as if they're waiting to swallow the player.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/3db3d72532f733ccab1f898ccff26568c8ff6a45.jpeg[/img]

Apart from conveying atmosphere, they also have a functional aspect: does it lead to a lethal or non-lethal map? How many players are needed to open the portal? Is everybody channeling?

[b]DM:[/b] It was important to us to let players interact with these entrances in a meaningful way. The new portal responds to the group: they are no longer clicking on a static portal, but a living one. If I finish my first channel, a specific rune will glow, if the team is completely finished the whole thing starts to open up, the world turns red and so on. This makes the whole experience of entering a Hellgate more interactive and immersive.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/0432dc59650f1c7f26e3dcdf8c1d16dfad1186ac.jpeg[/img]

[b]Once inside, the new Hellgates have much more diverse and varied environments than the old ones. What principles did you use in creating these new levels?[/b]

[b]SW:[/b] We created 10 different maps, each with a unique layout to offer more variety for both PvE and PvP. To give each a unique character, some are more open natural arenas with lava falls, some are claustrophobic caves or hell-fortresses, some are more cooled-down, some are hot as… well, you know. They offer different blockers and choke points but still support fair starting positions for groups of all sizes. And the new rising lava feature had to be considered, which shrinks the fighting zone and creates growing tension during fights.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/b7f389965cc568dcd0dd123d6a5cc9388081b03a.jpeg[/img]

[b]DM:[/b] We wanted to give players the feeling of physically moving through hell, going from the hill to the fort and after that to the traverse. We wanted to show a difference between “natural” hell and “architectural” hell. Additionally we followed quite a few guidelines to create interesting PvP moments. Try to encourage west-to-east combat, offer more than one way through a choke. In some maps we also willingly violated some of our rules to create a more characteristic element, as in the Traverse, which is basically one very long choke.

[b]What are some of the architectural features found in the new Hellgates?[/b]

[b]SW:[/b] We have some spiky hellish architectural elements like stairs, columns and railings – at least what demons would call architecture. With these we created larger structures like bridges, and reassembled them to make a variety of spaces and situations.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/63df53aa45641310151882853be5849ad7233894.jpeg[/img]

[b]DM:[/b] In the old Hellgates, we only had stairs for architecture, which made the maps fairly bleak. We wanted to give the demon faction more refinement and culture, so we added more architectural elements. For now it's just a few things like railings and pillars, but even these minor elements allowed us to build layouts that tell stories, such as the Fortress or Citadel.

[i]For more details of the Call to Arms update, see the official [url=https://albiononline.com/en/update/call-to-arms][b]update page[/b][/url][/i].

notes.title: Dev Talk: Hellgate Rework
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32445805/1741dcae47713c8fc6b32553812201a49053bc92.jpg[/img]
The Call to Arms update arrives March 17, and along with other major features like the Faction Warfare rework, this update includes a complete re-envisioning of [b]Hellgates[/b]. In our newest Dev Talk, Game and Level Designer Dominik Müller discusses the changes coming to Hellgates and some of the goals behind them.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=basSk2iTXDY
Prefer a written summary? Then read on...
[h3]A Core Albion Feature[/h3]
Hellgates have been around since the early days of the game, and exemplify one of Albion’s core concepts: tough PvP with high risk and high rewards. To bring Hellgates up to date in terms of mechanics and balancing while opening them up to more players, we did the following:
[list]	[*]Made Hellgate [b]PvE [/b]more entertaining with a much greater [b]variety of mobs[/b][/*]	[*]Added a huge variety of [b]map layouts[/b] that support different playstyles[/*]	[*]Implemented a [b]matchmaking system[/b] to ensure worthy opponents[/*]	[*]Added a new [b]lava mechanic[/b] that ensures fights eventually happen[/*]	[*]Created a whole new [b]10v10 Hellgate mode[/b] where large groups can fight for even bigger rewards[/*][/list]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/197957d83787be369fe313eab02e61d9af557fa3.jpeg[/img]
[h3]How They Work[/h3]
Previously, entering a Hellgate required killing a demon at a preset, static location. With the new system, Hellgates are accessed via [b]Hellgate Maps[/b], which can be crafted at the Artifact Foundry, looted from mobs, or bought. Like Dungeon Maps, they only work in zones appropriate to the map type; the Hellgate then spawns several zones away to maintain the danger of reaching the entrance.

Entering a Hellgate requires the following:
[list]	[*]Sufficient [b]base item power[/b], a new stat that [b]only[/b] measures your gear's tier, quality, and the enchantment while ignoring Mastery and Specialization levels, to ensure you no longer encounter players in overcharged 4.1 gear[/*]	[*]A [b]party size[/b] matching the Hellgate (2, 5, or 10 players respectively)[/*]	[*]Channelling to enter is [b]no longer interrupted by damage[/b], so preventing someone from entering is more challenging[/*][/list]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/a87e158857dc8b1e106080e5ae61316a01002dec.jpeg[/img]
[h3]New Layouts and Monsters[/h3]
Once inside, you'll encounter one of [b]ten completely new Hellgate layouts[/b] at random. These add a variety of different features: some have chokes, others have varying altitudes, and yet others are vast and open.

Matchmaking is based on the average [b]Hellgate Infamy[/b] of your party (see below). You have a chance of joining another party's Hellgate instantly; if no suitable opponent is found, you will enter your own Hellgate. The matchmaking criteria grow wider with time, until eventually another team enters your Hellgate or you enter theirs.

To complete a Hellgate, you can kill mobs until an [b]Infamy threshold[/b] is reached. Depending on which Hellgate layout you are in, you will find different mobs and minibosses, and occasionally a boss with huge rewards. If another party enters the Hellgate, all mobs (other than those guarding chests or shrines) will disappear.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/0432dc59650f1c7f26e3dcdf8c1d16dfad1186ac.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Lava[/h3]
Once two teams are in the same map, a new [b]rising lava[/b] mechanic will occur:
[list]	[*]After sufficient time passes, [b]lava [/b]appears at the edge of the map and moves towards the center[/*]	[*]The first part of the lava is a [b]warning zone[/b] that causes less damage[/*]	[*]The second part of the lava causes [b]drastically more damage[/b][/*]	[*]To avoid a stun/CC combo meta, players will become [b]immune to crowd control effects[/b] once they have been in the lava for a short time[/*]	[*]The lava [b]pauses [/b]after enclosing a final area at the center[/*]	[*]If more time passes without a winner, the lava [b]starts encroaching again[/b] until only one party is left[/*]	[*]Defeating an enemy team causes the lava to [b]disappear[/b] and [b]completes the Hellgate[/b], allowing your party to continue onward or return to the surface[/*][/list]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/8d3cde019526f73760c3ff4fda3109bbe21f3ed4.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Completing a Hellgate[/h3]
After killing enough demons or defeating an opposing party, your Hellgate will be [b]complete [/b]and a marker will appear on your minimap. If you kill an enemy party, you will be rewarded with an additional chest. Here you will find an [b]exit portal [/b]and another [b]entry gate[/b]. The portal will bring you back to the surface, while the gate lets you [b]chain[/b] into a new Hellgate if you meet the same IP and group size requirements as before.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/ebc18641b5b95da8e18ed3d4bd9728bc768697ed.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Infamy and IP Caps[/h3]
[b]Infamy [/b]works similarly to Corrupted Dungeons but is independent, with separate Infamy rankings for 2v2, 5v5, and 10v10 Hellgates:
[list]	[*]The higher your Infamy, the better the loot in the corresponding Hellgate type and the higher Infamy [b]opponents[/b] you will encounter[/*]	[*]As mentioned earlier, the longer you remain unmatched in a Hellgate, the wider the matchmaking criteria become until you eventually find a match[/*]	[*]Killing players [b]steals a portion of their Infamy and adds it to yours[/b] (and vice versa)[/*][/list]
(Note: with IP caps and requirements, we tried to strike a balance between keeping Hellgates competitive and making them more inclusive; we will keep a close eye on player feedback and adjust these numbers if needed.)

That's all for today - we hope you're as excited about the new Hellgates as we are, and that you are looking forward to testing yourself against your fellow adventurers when the Call to Arms update goes live on March 17. Thanks for watching!

notes.title: Animated Vegetation: A Closer Look
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/8cab9dbc84c109f8ae6df8c734f79cb72b3695b3.jpeg[/img]

The Call to Arms update arrives on March 17, bringing numerous major features and quality-of-life improvements. Among the latter is animated vegetation, which brings Albion's flowers, grass, bushes and trees to life across all five biomes. We spoke with Art Director [b]Marcus Koch[/b] and FX Artist [b]John Schroeter[/b] about this new feature.

[b]What was the goal of this visual upgrade to Albion's plant life?[/b]

[video autoplay="yes" loop="yes" muted="yes" playsinline="yes"]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/e83b7bdd39776dd3045739bdb275a806add1358c.mp4[/video]

These improvements will give players a much greater level of immersion while exploring the world. Traveling through a living, breathing environment feels far more natural and rewarding than experiencing a static one, and in many cases the visual elements of the biomes did not quite live up to what the audio was suggesting.

[b]The effect is especially striking in vegetation-heavy biomes such as forests. What were some of the steps you took to make the movement of trees, bushes, and grass more lifelike?[/b]

[video autoplay="yes" loop="yes" muted="yes" playsinline="yes"]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/2fe72799dafbe09fba28c4a63ff4236cd1f54c2e.mp4[/video]

We realized that having everything move the same amount would distract the players' attention, especially if huge trees (which are closer to the camera) were shaking too much. That's why vegetation closer to the ground, such as grass, moves more forcefully than the treetops do. 

Ultimately this helps keep the focus on the player character's level, where the game's action takes place. 

[i]For more details of everything coming with Call to Arms, check out the [url=https://albiononline.com/en/update/call-to-arms][b]update page[/b][/url].[/i]

notes.title: An Introduction to Guild Seasons
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32445805/c98b96ab45a895ad06e09930ca1cd5ce4b80d254.jpg[/img]

Being a member of a guild is one of the most rewarding parts of Albion Online. Grouping up, engaging in warfare, and conquering your own piece of Albion is all a part of the rich tapestry of the game. In this video, we'll cover all the basics of Guild Seasons, or you can read on for a summary.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1LKXoCgPxOY
[h3]The Basics[/h3]
In Albion, warfare between guilds takes place during [b]Guild Seasons[/b]. While a season is active, guilds can earn points to compete on the season leaderboard, allowing them to measure themselves against other guilds and compete for a variety of different [b]rewards[/b]. These rewards range from basic avatars and avatar rings all the way to Crystal Battle Mounts, 90-day Fame buffs, and even a statue honoring your guild in town!

The ranking tiers are as follows:
[list]	[*][b]Crystal: 250,000 Season Points[/b][/*]	[*][b]Gold: 80,000 Season Points[/b][/*]	[*][b]Silver: 25,000 Season Points[/b][/*]	[*][b]Bronze: 7,500 Season Points[/b][/*]	[*][b]Iron: 1,000 Season Points[/b][/*][/list]
There are set rewards for each rank, as well as special rewards for the [b]top 5 guilds[/b] of the season. (You can check out the specific rewards [url=https://albiononline.com/en/news/season-12-brings-incredible-new-rewards][b]here[/b][/url]).

[b]Note[/b]: In order to receive the rewards a guild has earned in a season, you must be a member of the guild for [b]75%[/b] of the season and also have Premium [b]active[/b] when the season ends.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/452d9ebf3bf611fd6e5b12ccd9c2f54dc791fef6.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Season Structure[/h3]
Seasons consist of three sections, starting with and separated by [b]Invasion Days[/b]. On Invasion Days, all Outlands territories lose their owners and are available to claim at one of two times based on their primetimes:
[list]	[*]EU Territories (12,15,18 and 21 UTC) are available to claim at [b]18:00 UTC on Saturday[/b][/*]	[*]NA Territories (00, 03 and 05 UTC) are available to claim at [b]01:00 UTC on Sunday[/b][/*][/list]
There are two further [b]Invasion Days[/b] each season, and the final portion of the season rewards [b]double points[/b] for all open world activities (territories, castles, etc).

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/599e830da9e5ef1cb10fc01160d557357baa640a.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Earning Points For Your Guild[/h3]
[b][u]Solo Players[/u][/b]

Even alone, you can help your guild progress in the rankings. As you earn keys towards your[b] Adventurer’s Challenge[/b], these will also credit your [b]Guild Challenge[/b] (excluding the 50,000 point daily bonus). Guild Challenges have 100 increasingly difficult levels with each one awarding Season Points.

[b][u]Small Groups [/u][/b]
[list]	[*][b]Mage Raids[/b]: Raiding territories not owned by your alliance and killing [b]Siphoning Mages[/b] steals Season Points from the guild that owns the territory. BEWARE: the guild will be notified the mages are under and attack and may come to defend them. The mages themselves also have a number of combat skills that you will need to be prepared for. Siphoning Mages generate more points the closer they are to the center of the Outlands.[/*]	[*][b]PvE[/b]: World Bosses (in zones marked on the map) and major bosses in Outlands static dungeons also give Season Points. As with mages and territories, the bosses nearer the center of the Outlands are worth more.[/*]	[*][b]Castle Outposts[/b]: Outlands Castle Outposts generate points every three hours for the guild that owns them. Bring demolition hammers, break down the doors and defeat the guards to claim them for your own![/*][/list]
[b][u]Large Groups[/u][/b]
[list]	[*]Large forces can conquer [b]territories[/b] and [b]castles[/b] to gain Season Points.[/*]	[*][b]Territories[/b]: see next section.[/*]	[*][b]Castles[/b]: these major objectives score points 4 times per day (0:00, 6:00, 12:00, and 18:00 UTC). The guild that owns the castle will receive points when the timer hits. Castles nearer the center of the Outlands are worth more points than those on the outer edge.[/*][/list]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/6e83d4590d02964b61e4959a2d58412b24d73848.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Territories and Season Points[/h3]
Outlands territories have a number of mechanics to generate season points for both the guild holding them and hostile forces:
[list]	[*]The primary mechanic is the [b]Siphoning Mages[/b] that spawn on a tower. Up to 4 can be spawned at once and they will continuously generate Season Points (current/max points visible via the worldmap).[/*]	[*]If 4 mages are kept alive for a full 24 hour period, the guild earns full points. If enemies raid and kill mages, less points will be earned.[/*]	[*]Mages can also be made to generate more points and made more powerful by leveling the [b]tower [/b]up through [b]Crystal League[/b] matches. Points are paid out to the owning guild at the beginning of the territory's timer.[/*]	[*]As you move towards the center of the Outlands, towers become more valuable but also have an additional mechanic known as [b]points storage[/b]. This only applies to territories above a certain value (distance from the outer ring).[/*]	[*]When these territories earn points, the listed percentage (ranging from 10-35%) is put into storage instead of paid out to the guild.[/*]	[*]Stored points are paid in full [b]to the guild owning the territory[/b] on the next [b]invasion day [/b]or [b]season end[/b]. If the territory is conquered by another guild before this happens, the new owner immediately receives 10% of points stored, and another 10% are lost.[/*][/list]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/4612d65b913b2af4cc105414e85aa77bc69a0c97.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Crystal League Matches and Season Points[/h3]
Guilds can earn Season Points via 5v5 or 20v20 [b]Crystal League Battles[/b]. The higher the match level, the more points it gives. The total available points are split between the winners and losers based on final score, with the winning team receiving all points if they win by a large enough margin.

The following points are available [b]per player, per match[/b] for Crystal League matches:

[b][u]5v5 Matches:[/u][/b]
[list]	[*]Level 1: 1 Point[/*]	[*]Level 2: 5 Points[/*]	[*]Level 3: 15 Points[/*]	[*]Level 4: 40 Points[/*]	[*]Level 5: 100 Points[/*]	[*]Level 6: 250 Points[/*]	[*]Level 7: 600 Points[/*]	[*]Level 8: 1600 Points[/*]	[*]Level 9: 5000 Points[/*][/list]
[b][u]20v20 Matches:[/u][/b]
[list]	[*]Level 1: 5 Points[/*]	[*]Level 2: 10 Points[/*]	[*]Level 3: 15 Points[/*]	[*]Level 4: 60 Points[/*]	[*]Level 5: 200 Points[/*]	[*]Level 6: 750 Points[/*]	[*]Level 7: 2500 Points[/*][/list]
Because the points are on a per-player basis, a team does not need to consist of one guild's members. Mixed teams can score points for their individual guilds, but uniting under one banner can generate a lot of points for that guild. To prevent guilds from simply amassing Crystal League teams and ignoring open-world content, there is a [b]maximum limit[/b] to the Crystal League points a guild can earn in a day (for both 5v5 and 20v20).

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/df1d2b6bc19e96e5bd597d41e3a3e242b245f566.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Alliances and Season Points[/h3]
Being allied with other guilds can bring additional strength and support but comes with some downsides.
[list]	[*]Firstly, you will have to [b]split [/b]a share of the season points you earn with the rest of your allies: 50% of the points goes to the guild that scored them, the other 50% is split between [b]ALL [/b]members of the alliance, [b]INCLUDING [/b]the guild that scored them.	[list]		[*]Example 1: Guild A is allied only with Guild B. If Guild A earns 100 points, they get 75 (50 for their own half, 25 for their share of the alliance split). Guild B receives 25 points.[/*]		[*]Example 2: Guild A is allied with Guilds B, C, D and E. If Guild A earns 100 points, they get 60 (50 for their own half, 10 for their share of the alliance split). Guilds B, C, D and E get 10 points each.[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]There are also penalties for Alliances who own [b]more than 10 territories[/b]: they will lose some Siphoned Energy (but not Season Points), and even start to lose a percentage of Fame and Silver gain if they pass 20 territories.[/*][/list]
Hopefully this guide has given you a solid overview of the mechanics of guild seasons, and some ideas as to how you can score points for your guild. Thanks for watching!

notes.title: Dev Talk: Loadouts
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32445805/245b74bddfb4ef32dd9c480da9d7726dde5888f9.jpg[/img]
The [b]Call to Arms[/b] update arrives March 17, and in addition to major reworks of Faction Warfare and Hellgates, also brings big quality-of-life improvements. Foremost among these is the new [b]Loadouts[/b] system. In our newest Dev Talk, UI Designer Moritz Bokelmann gives further details of this feature. (If you missed our earlier overview of the update, you can watch it [url=https://albiononline.com/en/news/devtalk-call-to-arms-introduction][b]here[/b][/url]).

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rn-feOUbBug
Prefer a written summary? Then read on...

Albion's “You are what you wear” system gives incredible freedom but also comes with some drawbacks. Getting killed and having to run back to a bank or chest to regear is time-consuming and keeps you out of the action, and even if you’re not into PvP, switching gear for different activities can be a hassle. To address this, we've introduced [b]Loadouts[/b].
[h3]The Basics[/h3][list]	[*]Loadouts are [b]saved sets of equipment, spells, and additional inventory items[/b][/*]	[*]Loadouts can be [b]quickly equipped[/b] from banks, chests and battlevaults[/*]	[*]Loadouts can be [b]shared with other players[/b][/*]	[*]Each Loadout includes [b]precise user-defined rules[/b] that allow for flexibility in the overall selection[/*]	[*]Loadouts are accessed via a new [b]Loadouts UI window[/b] in the Player Menu (click playername or Hotkey “L”)[/*]	[*][b]30 total slots[/b] are available and the list can be [b]searched and reordered[/b] freely[/*][/list]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/794cbd092105642db100639da409a5952bc23e68.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Creating Loadouts[/h3][list]	[*]To create a Loadout, click [b]any available slot[/b][/*]	[*]Select a [b]name, color and icon[/b][/*]	[*]Choose to start either from [b]currently equipped gear[/b] or [b]completely from scratch[/b][/*]	[*]If you use your current gear, all current [b]spell selections[/b] will also be saved[/*]	[*]You can then [b]freely edit[/b] the items in your Loadout, update spells, and add additional items[/*]	[*]The item list on the left contains [b]all tradeable items[/b] and can be filtered and searched as in the Marketplace[/*][/list]
The Loadout window also provides a preview of the [b]stats[/b] and [b]estimated market cost[/b] in the small flyout on the right side of the UI.
[h3]Setting Rules and Equipping[/h3]
Once you are happy with the Loadout, you can set rules for [b]how flexible the system can be[/b] when choosing which items to equip. You have three options:
[list]	[*][b]Exact[/b]: all parameters must be met exactly[/*]	[*][b]Same or Higher[/b]: tries to match exactly, then allows higher tiers, enchantments, etc.[/*]	[*][b]Same or Lower[/b]: tries to match exactly, then allows lower tiers, enchantments, etc.[/*]	[*]These are essentially [b]filter options[/b] applied when a bank or chest is searched[/*]	[*]Loadouts can be equipped from any [b]bank, chest, or battlevault[/b] you have access to, provided it contains any matching items[/*]	[*]To equip, open the container, choose a Loadout, and press "Equip"[/*][/list][h3]Sharing Loadouts[/h3]
Loadouts can be [b]shared[/b] via chat or ingame mail:
[list]	[*]Click “[b]Share Loadout[/b]” within main Loadout view[/*]	[*]Select sharing option[/*]	[*]Add any additional text desired[/*]	[*]Click to create a simplified version of the Loadout that can be saved into other players' lists[/*][/list]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/693ed1dccc5d0b7a2422854620bd0bd0c4102e02.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Guild Loadouts[/h3]
Guilds also have access to dedicated [b]Guild Loadouts[/b], which are similar to personal Loadouts with a few differences:
[list]	[*]Guilds have access to [b]100 slots[/b] for Loadouts[/*]	[*]Creating and editing requires “[b]Manage Guild Loadouts[/b]” access right[/*]	[*]Guild Loadouts behave like a guild's [b]library of preferred sets[/b] for various activities[/*]	[*]Using Guild Loadouts requires saving them into your personal Loadout list[/*][/list][h3]Use Cases[/h3]
[b]Case 1: High-level PvP (ZvZs, Crystal League, etc.)[/b]

You can create a Loadout with the absolute best items in the game via filtering the item list. Simply set everything to the highest available tier, enchantment level and quality, and potentially add Siphoned Energy for overcharging. You can then set all rules to “[b]Same or lower[/b]”, effectively creating a master-class set and telling the system to choose the closest possible items.

[b]Case 2: Lower-level PvP/PvE (Arena, Expeditions, etc.)[/b]
You could build these sets to match the required item power and set all rules to “[b]Same or higher[/b]”, which would do the exact opposite of Case 1 above: guarantee that you equip the most basic set of items that still meets the [b]minimum requirements[/b].

[b]Case 3: Hybrid / item-centered[/b]

Perhaps you want a cheap tier 4 set, but with a [b]tier 6 weapon[/b] to access all available spells. This is possible by simply experimenting and finding the correct Loadout setup for your needs.

[b]Case 4: Non-combat activities (crafting, farming, etc.)[/b]
A perfect example of this is a [b]crafter setup[/b] that only contains a mount, bag, and lots of salads. Then just all the materials you need for your daily crafting activities into the Loadout inventory.

These are just a few examples of things you can do with Loadouts, and we are very curious to see what other ideas you come up with.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/7ba7049b5d11ea0faa34ade8897c596bea379e69.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Additional Features: Coming Soon[/h3]
We are working hard to add Loadouts to the [b]Marketplace[/b], so you can directly purchase full sets, and hope to add this feature soon after the launch of Call to Arms. We are also looking into adapting the [b]Character Builder[/b] on the Albion website to make global sharing of Loadouts much easier. And of course we are very interested in the ideas that you, the players, have for this feature, so feel free to reach out and share your thoughts.

Thanks for watching!

notes.title: Artwork Showcase: Caerleon Faction
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/2e821c3516484b001f38de1b916ea6b218ccb35a.jpeg[/img]

The [b]Call to Arms[/b] update arrives March 17, bringing a completely reworked Faction Warfare system with a new playable [b]Caerleon Faction[/b]. In our newest art showcase, Marcus Koch, Art Director of Albion Online, describes the process of creating new NPCs, enemies, and Outposts based on the Caerleon mythos, and shows off some of the concepts that defined this new "outlaw Faction".

[b]What was the main style / aesthetic you were trying to convey with the design of the Caerleon faction?[/b]

As the Caerleon Faction differs from the other Factions where no PvP between members is allowed, we wanted to present this Faction in a darker and more twisted way. We took inspiration from the real-life Thirty Years' War, an age where soldiers fought amongst themselves in loose bands and many things had to be improvised.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/ac940420d15564f2c759283c9b9e7aa28ddfebdc.jpeg[/img]

[b]Does this improvised, patchwork aesthetic extend to the updated Caerleon visuals as well?[/b]

Caerleon's wealthy past has given way to a fallen present, and the city is a mix of ancient ruins and newer structures, cut through with crooked alleys. It's a place where riches can be earned quickly and lost even quicker, so everyone keeps one hand on their weapon at all times, and one eye over their shoulder.

[b]Any hints of details players should look out for?[/b]

If you just walk the side alleys you might encounter some little shadows scurrying around… and you might be surprised who is visiting the tavern and lurking around for a drink or two.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/9e64b4565abd6505036eb49a97de6f463b1e8d94.jpeg[/img]

[b]How did the design of the "Stabbed Mug" tavern come to be?[/b]

We wanted this Faction Base to look less “official”. Here you get your contract in a less formal way, and a dirty medieval tavern just felt like the right place in a rough town such as Caerleon. If you enlist here, you're doing it to line your own pocket instead of someone else's. As long as you can keep it :)

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/b7df9d17ebe34e4817fd631bf73517e367ff0337.png[/img]

[b]From concept to modeling to animation to audio, it takes a whole team to create Albion's world. Kudos to the Art Team for bringing this new Faction to life![/b]

notes.title: The Season 12 Patch is Here
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/657cfe6697cfbc182f378490b2ddf239751efbc4.jpeg[/img]

Guild Season 12 kicks off on [b]Saturday, March 13[/b]. In anticipation of this, [b]Rise of Avalon Patch 15[/b], AKA the [b]Season 12 Patch[/b], brings changes to make ownership of territories more significant and create incentives for more Outlands activities outside of large-scale battles. It also brings improvements to the new 20v20 Crystal League alongside other improvements and fixes.

Here's a rundown of what's new:
[h3]Season Point Changes[/h3][list]	[*][b]Territory Season Points[/b] are still given [b]daily[/b] for owned Outlands territories, and have been [b]increased[/b] overall, with the point difference between the outer and inner parts of the Outlands somewhat flattened[/*]	[*][b]Castle Season Points[/b] are still given [b]every six hours[/b] for owned castles and have been [b]increased[/b] overall[/*]	[*][b]Castle Outpost Season Points[/b] are now given [b]every three hours[/b] for owned Outposts and have likewise been [b]increased[/b] overall[/*][/list][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/9c4a363d95435364b9af2c12b18aa6e22588168c.png[/img]
[h3]World Boss and Static Dungeon Changes[/h3]
The PvE Fame buff in these locations now comes primarily from [b]Elite mobs[/b] instead of the bosses themselves, and stacks incrementally with each mob killed. By repeatedly defeating mobs in the area, players in a party can stack the buff up to [b]+50% bonus Fame[/b] while remaining in the zone.
[h3]Other Changes[/h3][list]	[*][b]20v20 Crystal League Changes:[/b] Starting Points per team and point value per player kill increased, new level added between the former Levels 1 and 2 – there are now 7 total levels[/*]	[*][b]Treasure Chest Changes:[/b] Overall loot value of Castle Chests increased, and Lesser Outland Treasure Chests now spawn more often[/*]	[*][b]Guild Challenge Change:[/b] Reduced Season Points for lower Guild Challenge levels put more emphasis on open-world objectives like territories[/*]	[*][b]Bracket Season Point Thresholds Updated:[/b] The points required for each bracket (Crystal, Gold, etc.) have been updated in tandem with these changes[/*]	[*][b]Fixes:[/b] Corrected map tooltips for Outlands treasures and fixed some cases where Hideouts could not be set as Home[/*][/list]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/362707882da027970bd1ce1398291dc467c5f50c.jpeg[/img]

For the full list of fixes, changes, and improvements, check out the [url=https://albiononline.com/en/changelog/RISE%20OF%20AVALON%20PATCH%2015][b]official Patchnotes[/b][/url].

For the Season 12 Schedule, [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/144466-Guild-Season-12-Schedule/][b]click here[/b][/url].

notes.title: The Keeper Challenge Returns!
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/9fade3d422c0bb7bdfc7f574d635d1be092368ac.jpeg[/img]

Spring is back, and the Keepers of Albion are beginning to awaken... and for the entire month of March, you can take the [b]Keeper Challenge[/b] to collect fantastic rewards! Earn points for open-world activities, unlock chests to get valuable loot, and claim your very own [b]Grizzly Bear mount[/b].

[img]https://i.imgur.com/FdTDY3p.png[/img]
[b]GRIZZLY BEAR:[/b] This month's Challenge brings back the popular [b]Grizzly Bear[/b], a huge, intimidating mount with an arsenal of powerful spells. In addition to its Intimidating Aura toggle spell, it also gains a temporary [b]speed boost[/b] when attacked, giving its rider an edge when enemies are in pursuit.
 
[img]https://i.imgur.com/dg76ds8.png[/img]
[b]AVATAR RING:[/b] Reach your goals to unlock the [b]Keeper Challenge avatar ring[/b], which gives your chosen avatar the stone-and-leather look of Albion's true guardians. This non-tradable item permanently unlocks this avatar border for one character, or can be traded for one [b]Adventurer's Token[/b] at the Vanity Merchant.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/C4sRQZo.png[/img]
[b]SEASONAL SPECIALS:[/b] All month, reach weekly goals to unlock [b]Keeper Challenge chests[/b]. In addition to valuable rewards like Adventurer's Tomes, Silver bags, and rare resources, this month's chests contain various [b]Keeper-themed furniture and capes[/b].

As always, you can earn Challenge Points by [b]gathering, fishing, farming, and killing monsters[/b]. Points count simultaneously toward a daily bonus, a weekly unlockable chest, and the monthly mount. So log in, head out into the open world, gather points, and claim your rewards!

notes.title: Season 12 Brings Incredible New Rewards
notes.content:
Albion Online's twelfth Guild Season starts on [b]Saturday, March 13[/b]. Guilds that reach a high enough rank during the season can claim fantastic rewards including an [b]avatar[/b], [b]avatar ring[/b], and the powerful new [b]Juggernaut[/b] mount!

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/c4a125b30a54e47c723340e8389667f526805e5a.png[/img]

The Juggernaut is a powerful engage tank for large-scale battles. While it has little impact on smaller player groups, its full potential is unleashed when facing large enemy armies, where it can summon a whirling tornado of rocks. This mount will be awarded to guilds who reach [b]Silver Rank or higher[/b] during Season 12, with increasingly higher stats (and increasingly epic appearance) with each successive tier.

The winning guild will receive a statue among the past Guild Season winners in Conquerors' Hall and members of the top three guilds will receive their own placeable Winner Statue. Qualifying guilds will also receive other goodies like an avatar and avatar ring, a Fame Bonus, and more:

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/10319110fb1ac1686582dc6982f0587abfd9f310.jpeg[/img]

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/60296c6aa40d4dfc6f90c4cb05c9aacab416f52c.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Season 12 Changes[/h3]
[b]Season Points[/b] from Territories, Castles, and Castle Outposts have been updated and rebalanced for Season 12. The PvE Fame Buff in [b]open-world boss locations[/b] has been reworked, and Lesser Outlands Treasure Chests now spawn more often. A new level has been added to the [b]20v20 Crystal League[/b] and Guild Challenge rewards have been rebalanced. And updates to the [b]Smart Cluster Queue[/b] and [b]Hideout defense[/b] will follow in a patch after the season begins.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/ea19b7ec31fb01f6f29d799212929e008ec74b2a.jpeg[/img]

For the full list of changes, see [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/144464][b]this forum post[/b][/url]. Click [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/144466][b]here[/b][/url] for the complete season schedule.

notes.title: Call to Arms Arrives March 17
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/87b91f7f5558ad17f639b83ffbfca12aab3f6bd4.jpeg[/img]

It's official: on [b]March 17, 2021[/b], the [b]Call to Arms[/b] update goes live! Call to Arms is Albion's tenth major content update since launch, and brings a host of major new features. The centerpiece of the update is a complete re-envisioning of Albion's [b]Faction Warfare[/b] system, which gives a sense of truly belonging to a City Faction, as well as a major expansion of the [b]Royal Continent[/b]. A fully reworked and expanded [b]Hellgate[/b] system brings new life to one of Albion's most thrilling and intense PvP settings, and numerous additional [b]upgrades, fixes, and quality-of-life improvements[/b] make the world of Albion better than ever before.
[h3]Faction Warfare Re-Envisioned[/h3]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/2c6321d9f3df900f9a7d8415ce765ddf0a251c7a.jpeg[/img]

The new system allows Factions to take not just Outposts but entire regions as well, and rewards loyalty to a chosen Faction via updated [b]Faction ranks[/b] and month-long [b]Faction Campaigns[/b] with valuable rewards. [b]Caerleon[/b] joins the fight as a fully playable sixth Faction with a unique "lawless" playstyle. Alongside the six regular Faction Mounts, each city now has its own [b]Elite Faction Mount[/b] with powerful abilities.

To accommodate Albion's growing population and provide more space for Faction Warfare to play out, the [b]Royal Continent[/b] has been greatly expanded with numerous new regions, and a recurring [b]Bandit Invasion[/b] event in the red zones offers thrilling large-scale combat for members of all Factions.
[h3]Hellgates 2.0[/h3][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/dffe36cf0c3bcb3687bfed2057eb626260504446.jpeg[/img]
Call to Arms brings major upgrades to [b]Hellgates[/b], introducing ten all-new Hellgate layouts and new demonic foes for varied and engaging PvE. Hellgate PvP takes on new dimensions as well, with the ability to [b]chain Hellgates[/b] after a win and a [b]rising lava[/b] mechanic that ensures a final showdown. And last but not least, new [b]10v10 Hellgates[/b] offer thrilling, high-stakes group PvP for new and veteran players alike.
[h3]Loadouts, Tooltips, and More[/h3][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/d42231ded770618b394c05541d586967cc4b002a.jpeg[/img]
Call to Arms brings major quality-of-life improvements like [b]Loadouts[/b], which allow players to create and equip pre-selected builds, and updated [b]ability tooltips[/b]. [b]Animated vegetation[/b] brings new visual life to Albion's biomes, and numerous additional improvements, fixes, balance changes, and optimizations have been implemented to make the world of Albion better than ever.

For more details, check out the official Update Page:
[h2][url=https://albiononline.com/en/update/call-to-arms]LEARN MORE[/url][/h2]

notes.title: Dev Talk: The Sixth Faction
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32445805/a4f083c66df232f736a2eaa84c14a62ea382dc49.jpg[/img]

In his third and final Dev Talk on the upcoming Faction Warfare rework, Game Director Robin Henkys gives a first look at the mysterious new Faction joining the fight. If you haven't yet watched the first two videos, you can check them out here:
[list]	[*][b]Part 1: [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dwTs_R95u_Q&t=0s]Faction Warfare Revamped[/url][/b][/*]	[*][b]Part 2: [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8eC73qrEFYw&t=0s]Faction Ranks and Elite Mounts[/url][/b][/*][/list]
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vBLdULJ-elA
Prefer a written summary? Then read on...
[h3]Caerleon Joins the Fight[/h3]
Since the fall of the Caerleon portal and the city’s resulting decline, Caerleon has become a nest of bandits, smugglers, rogues and mercenaries. Now the Council of Caerleon has decided to join the war between the cities and profit from the situation.

To represent this development, we’ve [b]reworked the layout and massively improved the graphics[/b] of the city. We've added the “Stabbed Mug” Tavern, where Mercenary Captain [b]Henry Cutter[/b] recruits unscrupulous souls to fight the other cities.
[h3]A Different Kind of Faction[/h3]
The Caerleon Faction offers [b]a different style of Faction gameplay[/b]:
[list]	[*]As with all Factions, fighting for Caerleon lets you engage other Factions without reputation loss[/*]	[*]However, you will also be able to engage (and be engaged by) [b]other players in the Caerleon Faction[/b][/*]	[*]You can capture other Factions' Outposts and regions as usual, but instead of generating value over time, these turn into [b]bandit camps[/b] which generate no defensive value[/*]	[*]Instead, Caerleon players can make huge profits plundering Outposts and regions, as captured points [b]are not shared with the Faction as a whole[/b][/*]	[*]Finally, Caerleon players need to beware of betrayal: should one bandit group become too dominant, the others will have to put a stop to it if they want any of the profits for themselves[/*][/list]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/2f488fd1b7d66981dc12acbf501e973235c035e0.jpeg[/img]

With this playstyle, Caerleon offers unique gameplay for veteran players looking for dynamic full-loot PvP with plenty of enemies.
[h3]What makes Caerleon worthwhile?[/h3]
In addition to the appeal of living free under your own banner, Caerleon offers unique Faction rewards of its own:
[list]	[*]Faction Points can buy [b]Caerleon Greywolf Pups[/b] or [b]Caerleon Elite Greywolf Pups[/b][/*]	[*]These can be grown into a [b]T5 Caerleon Greywolf[/b] or a [b]T8 Caerleon Elite Greywolf[/b] respectively[/*]	[*]Like other Elite Faction Mounts, the Elite Greywolf has two unique abilities:	[list]		[*][b]Hunter’s Mark[/b]: marks an enemy who then leaves behind a trail; collecting this trail boosts movement speed, with wounded targets offering a greater boost[/*]		[*][b]Faction ability - Spite[/b]: dismounts the rider and grants a damage reflection aura to nearby allies (can only be used while flagged for Caerleon, only affects Caerleon players in your party)[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Caerleon players can also purchase [b]crests [/b]to craft [b]Caerleon Faction capes[/b] with a powerful passive that resets your Q-ability for double casting[/*]	[*]Finally, [b]Trade missions[/b] are available which are more profitable than those of other Factions[/*][/list]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/8e6bbabf0a39d9011cad8f2b81ab6e359f58553f.jpeg[/img]
[h3]New Daily Event: Bandit Assault[/h3]
Additionally, the Caerleon Faction NPCs are responsible for the recurring “[b]Bandit Assault[/b]” event in Albion's red zones:
[list]	[*]Irregularly throughout the day, Factions will lose control of all Outposts and regions in the red zones, which will be taken over by Bandits[/*]	[*]Recapturing them is a top priority, as there will be a massive reward paid out to players in the Faction which has claimed the most regions during the event[/*]	[*]Although Caerleon players cannot participate in this event as a Faction, they can use the rush of Faction players into the red zones to set ambushes and find plenty of full-loot PvP[/*][/list][h3]In Conclusion[/h3]
This concludes our look at the all-new Faction Warfare system coming with the Call to Arms update. Will you join the Caerleon Faction and lead a life of villainy? Or will you proudly fly the banner of another city? We can’t wait to see which Faction will produce the mightiest heroes, and we're really looking forward to joining the battle ourselves.

Call to Arms will be released in mid-March – until then, stay tuned for more Dev Talks on new features!

notes.title: Dev Talk: Faction Ranks and Elite Mounts
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32445805/d09b2b2c5618ebafb21050cab99eb5f535fad443.jpg[/img]

[b]Call to Arms[/b], the next major update for Albion Online, will bring a complete revamp of the Faction Warfare system. In our [url=https://albiononline.com/en/news/devtalk-faction-warfare-revamped][b]last Dev Talk[/b][/url], Game Director Robin Henkys introduced the major components of this rework. This week, he gives a first look at Faction Campaigns, Faction Ranks, and rewards including new [b]Elite Faction Mounts[/b].

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8eC73qrEFYw
Prefer a written summary? Then read on...
[h3]The Faction Screen[/h3]
The [b]Faction Screen[/b] is accessed via the Activities button. It shows the current overall Faction rankings, as well as which Factions offer the best rewards for joining. Most importantly, it shows your personal [b]Faction Campaign[/b] progress and your current [b]Faction Rank[/b].

After enlisting with a Faction, you become eligible to fight in their [b]Campaign [/b]and climb the ranks. Campaigns are month-long seasons that count all points you earn on behalf of your Faction, and award chests with valuable loot as you reach certain milestones.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/a49d2fb50a3011591cfecb20f27508beb22d77be.jpeg[/img]

[b]Faction Ranks[/b] measure your [b]loyalty [/b]alongside your contribution. Lower ranks are the same for all Factions, but higher ranks are unique to each city and are extremely hard to unlock and maintain. We’re also working on showing which players currently rank highest within your Faction. Your rank affects the rate at which you earn points.
[h3]Faction Store + Elite Mounts[/h3]
Once you've earned points, you can still spend them on [b]City Faction Hearts[/b], [b]crests for Faction Capes[/b] and [b]Faction Mounts[/b]. We've significantly boosted Faction Mount stats, and we’ve added an [b]Elite version of each Faction mount[/b]. These offer new T8 rare mounts for animal breeders to grow, and come with [b]two unique abilities[/b] each.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/822e14c1de56b619c46895b83b16ceec4f968818.png[/img]

Note: Faction abilities are unlocked when the player is [b]flagged for the appropriate Faction[/b] and only affect players [b]in the same Faction[/b]:
[list]	[*][b]Lymhurst Elite Boar[/b]	[list]		[*][b]Regular ability[/b]: dash forward, damaging unmounted enemies and knocking them backwards[/*]		[*][b]Faction ability – Boar Vitality[/b]: dismount and give allies a large healing area of effect[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*][b]Bridgewatch Elite Terrorbird[/b]	[list]		[*][b]Regular ability[/b]: “Zig” to a targeted direction, then “Zag” to dash again and avoid attacks[/*]		[*][b]Faction ability – Desert Breeze[/b]: dismount and grant all allies a move speed bonus[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*][b]Martlock Elite Ram[/b]	[list]		[*][b]Regular ability[/b]: reduce damage taken while channeling, then gain move speed based on the number of hits taken[/*]		[*][b]Faction ability – Mountain Resilience[/b]: dismount and grant a Max Health bonus to allies in range[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*][b]Thetford Elite Swamp Salamander[/b]	[list]		[*][b]Regular ability[/b]: sheds its skin to cleanse any negative effects[/*]		[*][b]Faction ability – Reptile Agility[/b]: grants attack speed and damage bonuses to nearby allies[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*][b]Fort Sterling Elite Direbear[/b]	[list]		[*][b]Regular ability[/b]: passive that stacks with each attack, followed up with "Winter Call" ability that boosts move speed and slows enemies based on the stacks[/*]		[*][b]Faction ability – Frozen Defense[/b]: dismount and grant a defense bonus to allies in range[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
NOTE: These abilities are still in testing at the time of this recording and their functionality may change.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/748700128b9355b878c086a2ff0d50f17f9cb0cb.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Maximizing Faction Points[/h3]
In addition to earning points by fighting for your Faction, you can also see which Factions offer the most points. Factions that aren't doing as well offer [b]much higher rates of Faction Point gains[/b], and will even allow you to retain part of your [b]rank[/b] if you enlist with them. Successful Factions, however, have less reason to pay high rates of points and won’t be so welcoming to new recruits, so you’ll have to [b]give up your rank[/b] to join them. These mechanisms ensure Faction Warfare stays balanced and players have strong incentives to join cities in need, while leaving the choice of Faction ultimately up to you.

We covered a lot in this talk, but there’s still more to come. In the next video, we’ll unmask the [b]new Faction[/b], talk about their unique gameplay and rewards, and discuss the recurring [b]red zone event[/b].

Thanks for watching!

notes.title: Dev Talk: Faction Warfare Revamped
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32445805/7fb7051901dd473cccd751aa31ce90303064fcb6.jpg[/img]

In our newest Dev Talk, Albion's Game Director, Robin Henkys, introduces the major changes coming to [b]Faction Warfare[/b] with the [b]Call to Arms[/b] update. (Note: since this is a huge feature with lots to discuss, we'll have multiple videos covering this topic.)

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dwTs_R95u_Q
Prefer a written summary? Then read on...

As many of you know, Faction Warfare has been in the game for quite a while now. In this system players can sign up for one City Faction and go fight on behalf of their city against enemy Faction NPC and players. They can capture Outposts and earn Faction Points to spend on Faction rewards.

Key goals of the rework:
[list]	[*][b]Accessible and inclusive[/b] for all players on the Royal Continent[/*]	[*]Meaningful incentives for [b]loyalty to a city[/b][/*]	[*][b]Exciting large-scale battles[/b] that are easy to join and reward participation[/*]	[*][b]Supporting existing Faction Warfare players[/b] and ensuring their current full-loot system is continued and improved[/*][/list]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/1f54142b25e66aa50ffced08d8957b46f91501de.jpeg[/img]

So how will these goals be met?

[b]1. Accessible and inclusive:[/b]
[list]	[*]Faction Warfare in yellow and blue regions is now [b]non-lethal[/b], so new players can engage with this feature without losing their gear[/*]	[*]Faction Warfare in the red zones remains [b]lethal[/b][/*]	[*][b]Increased number of red zones[/b] in the world[/*]	[*]Red zones have [b]higher value Faction Point targets[/b] for advanced players[/*][/list]
[b]2. Faction loyalty:[/b]
[list]	[*]Enlistment and flagging up is now a [b]two-step process: [/b]	[list]		[*]Step 1: [b]enlist [/b]with a Faction to become a [b]permanent member[/b][/*]		[*]Step 2: [b]actively flag up[/b] to actually fight on their behalf[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]If you choose to un-flag, you will still remain enlisted[/*]	[*]As long as you remain enlisted, you will keep your rank and other advantages, encouraging loyalty to a chosen Faction[/*][/list]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/622099046cf8e00154df92eda43b901b60d821f5.jpeg[/img]

[b]3. Large-scale battles:[/b]
[list]	[*]Lets new players gain their first experience in open-world warfare, while veteran players can participate during periods of low guild activity[/*]	[*]Focuses on bringing opposing Factions into conflict via a “[b]front line[/b]”, where large battles occur frequently and players can easily join[/*]	[*]To achieve this, we made regions of the world map [b]conquerable[/b][/*]	[*]To conquer a region, a Faction needs to control and hold the majority of [b]Outposts [/b]within it[/*]	[*]Controlling a region allows you to push the front line further towards the enemy while protecting your own regions[/*]	[*]In yellow and blue regions, players knocked out can rejoin the battle from a nearby friendly Outpost, so retaining control of Outposts is critical[/*]	[*]Should a region get separated from the rest of your regions, you will no longer be able to respawn there, cutting you off from reinforcements[/*]	[*]Players can use this to their advantage by capturing regions strategically and breaking an enemy’s supply line[/*][/list]
[b]4. Faction rewards:[/b]
[list]	[*]Players will still be rewarded in [b]Faction Points[/b], which they can spend at their Faction stores[/*]	[*]Earn points by capturing [b]Outposts[/b] and [b]whole zones[/b][/*]	[*]The value of capturable objectives [b]increases over time[/b], offering an incentive to push behind enemy lines[/*]	[*]Players are also rewarded for [b]defense[/b], as regions generate more points the longer they are held[/*]	[*]In addition to immediate rewards, a [b]weekly report[/b] sums up your performance and rewards additional points based on personal and overall Faction success[/*][/list]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/b7aaeca205de812479df79ce01d520d79ae094d6.jpeg[/img]

[b]Notes on red zone play:[/b]
[list]	[*]Red zones give the same rewards, but in [b]much greater amounts[/b][/*]	[*]With no [b]respawning [/b]at Outposts, red-zone players will have to maneuver carefully and strategically[/*]	[*]In addition to generating much higher rewards, the red zones will have [b]a new enemy[/b] to be announced soon[/*][/list]
The Faction Warfare rework is so large we’ve split it into multiple videos – join us next time where we’ll discuss Faction Rewards, ranks, balancing, and the all new Faction Seasons.

Thanks for watching!

notes.title: Patch 13 is Here
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/dae55ab0fe0b3255e68e5de9b8ca7cf9534669ab.jpeg[/img]

Patch 13, AKA the [b]Rise of Avalon Balance Patch[/b], is now live! This patch brings numerous changes to Avalonian mobs, big meta changes to combat balancing, a long-awaited quality of life improvement, and more. Here's what's new:
[h3]Updated Avalonian Mobs[/h3]
Patch 13 improves the overall experience of [b]Elite Dungeons[/b], offering a more streamlined combat experience while fighting Avalonians while retaining the challenge of these high-level enemies. Most high-damage Avalonian spells can no longer be reflected, the Construct's "blind spot" has been removed, and the skills of the [b]High Priestess[/b], [b]Crystal Basilisk[/b], and [b]Sir Bedivere[/b] have been updated to keep you on your toes.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/911dc1ec75af35c531494c2ad247bc73d29b11d3.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Keeping the Meta Fresh[/h3]
This patch contains numerous changes to combat abilities across a wide range of weapons, armor, and equipment, with the primary goal of addressing the meta in[b] small-scale PvP[/b] and [b]Corrupted Dungeons[/b]. A new Mace ability, [b]Guard Rune[/b], has been added, the Guardian Helmet's Emergency Heal has been reworked as [b]Emergency Shield[/b], and several [b]Battle Mounts[/b] have reduced cooldowns to keep them competitive in open-world combat.
[h3]Rejoice: The Use-All Button is Here[/h3]
Free yourself from the tyranny of endless clicking, and use all your Silver Bags and Tomes with [b]a single button click[/b]. Patch 13 introduces the [b]Use All Button[/b], perhaps Albion's most-requested feature of all time. If you missed the teaser trailer, you can watch it in all its glory here:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=S5h8XjI9O0c
[h3]Additional Changes[/h3][list]	[*][b]Political View[/b] is once again available on the World Map[/*]	[*]Updates to setting a [b]Hideout [/b]as Home - details [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/143364][b]here[/b][/url][/*]	[*]Fixes to the [b]Estimated Market Value[/b] display[/*]	[*]Improvements and optimizations to the [b]mobile version[/b][/*]	[*]...and much more[/*][/list]
As always, you can read the full list of changes in the [url=https://albiononline.com/en/changelog/RISE%20OF%20AVALON%20PATCH%2013][b]official patchnotes[/b][/url].
